## Method

Each record was researched live from primary sources (official websites, repositories, release pages, documentation and security advisories) on its verification date. Claims that could not be verified live are listed under *Requires verification* and must not be presented as current. The data contract, research rules and scope ownership are defined in [`research/README.md`](research/README.md).

### Bitcoin Core

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | Full-node implementations |
| Purpose | Reference full-node implementation of the Bitcoin protocol: downloads, validates and relays blocks and transactions, and exposes JSON-RPC, REST and ZMQ interfaces, an optional descriptor wallet and the bitcoin-qt graphical interface. |
| Official website | <https://bitcoincore.org/> |
| Official repository | <https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin> |
| Maintenance status | active — Latest stable release 31.1 announced 2026-07-08 (files in /bin/bitcoin-core-31.1/ dated 2026-07-07). Maintained lines per the lifecycle page: 31.x, 30.x (30.3, 2026-07-08) and 29.x (29.4, announced 2026-07-13, GitHub release 2026-07-10) until 32.0 ships. 32.0rc1 tagged 2026-09-14 and 32.0rc4 on 2026-10-12 (target was 2026-10-10). Latest master commit 2026-10-20. Repository not archived. |
| Superseded by | — |
| Latest verified stable release | 31.1 (2026-07-08) — <https://bitcoincore.org/en/releases/31.1/> |
| Verification date | 2026-10-21 |
| Native Windows | yes |
| Windows versions | Windows 10 version 1903 or later for 31.x and 32.0 (29.x and 30.x release notes say Windows 10 or later) |
| Windows architectures | x64 |
| Windows distribution | Authenticode-signed NSIS installer (bitcoin-31.1-win64-setup.exe, 39 221 288 bytes) and signed portable ZIP (bitcoin-31.1-win64.zip, 54 894 985 bytes) from https://bitcoincore.org/bin/bitcoin-core-31.1/; unsigned variants (-win64-setup-unsigned.exe, -win64-unsigned.zip), a debug-symbols ZIP, a codesigning tarball and a torrent are also published. No Windows ARM64 build (Guix builds only x86_64-w64-mingw32). |
| WSL2 | likely |
| Docker | community-image |
| Other platforms | Linux tarballs for x86_64, aarch64, armhf, riscv64 and powerpc64 (glibc 2.31 or later, Linux kernel 3.17 or later); macOS 14 or later for 31.x (x86_64 and arm64 ZIP and tarball); Snap Store package; source builds for other Unix-like systems. |
| APIs and interfaces | `json-rpc`: JSON-RPC over HTTP POST on 127.0.0.1 and ::1, port 8332 mainnet, 18332 testnet3, 48332 testnet4, 38332 signet, 18443 regtest. Endpoints / and /wallet/<walletname>/ (mandatory when several wallets are loaded). JSON-RPC 1.1 behaviour by default; strict JSON-RPC 2.0 when the request contains "jsonrpc": "2.0" (since 28.0), including notifications (HTTP 204). Batch arrays are executed sequentially and always return HTTP 200. Enabled by default in bitcoind (-server=1), disabled by default in bitcoin-qt. 151 public methods in 31.1 plus 19 hidden ones; 32.0 adds getopenrpcinfo and rpc.discover (OpenRPC 1.4.1). — authentication: HTTP Basic. Default: cookie file .cookie in the network data directory containing __cookie__:<64 hex characters>, regenerated at every start and deleted on clean shutdown. Static credentials: rpcauth=<user>:<salt>$<HMAC-SHA256(key=salt, msg=password)> (share/rpcauth/rpcauth.py). rpcuser/rpcpassword still supported but logged as less secure. Optional per-user method allow-lists (rpcwhitelist, rpcwhitelistdefault). 250 ms delay after a failed login. No TLS. ([documentation](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/doc/JSON-RPC-interface.md))<br>`rest`: Unauthenticated read-only REST interface on the RPC listener when -rest=1 (default 0): /rest/tx, /rest/block, /rest/block/notxdetails, /rest/blockpart (31.0+), /rest/headers, /rest/blockfilter, /rest/blockfilterheaders, /rest/blockhashbyheight, /rest/spenttxouts (30.0+), /rest/chaininfo.json, /rest/deploymentinfo, /rest/getutxos, /rest/mempool/info.json and /rest/mempool/contents.json in bin, hex or json formats. — authentication: None. Exposed wherever the RPC listener is bound; upstream warns that a local browser can be abused to read node data. ([documentation](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/doc/REST-interface.md))<br>`zmq`: ZeroMQ PUB notifications (Windows release binaries include ZMQ): topics hashblock, hashtx, rawblock, rawtx and sequence, configured with -zmqpub<topic>=<address> and -zmqpub<topic>hwm (default 1000). Three-part messages: topic, body, 4-byte little-endian sequence number. No ports by default. — authentication: None; bind to loopback or a firewalled interface. ([documentation](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/doc/zmq.md))<br>`p2p`: Bitcoin peer-to-peer protocol on port 8333 mainnet, 18333 testnet3, 48333 testnet4, 38333 signet, 18444 regtest; BIP324 v2 encrypted transport on by default since 27.0; Tor onion, I2P (SAM) and CJDNS networks; inbound onion connections on 127.0.0.1:8334 by default (port + 1 when -port is set, since 29.0); PCP/NAT-PMP port mapping on by default since 30.0. ([documentation](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/doc/bips.md))<br>`cli`: bitcoin-cli (RPC client), the bitcoin wrapper command (30.0+: bitcoin node, gui, rpc, wallet, tx, util, test), bitcoin-wallet (offline wallet tool: info, create, dump, createfromdump), bitcoin-tx (raw transaction editor) and bitcoin-util (grind; getchainparams in 32.0). — authentication: bitcoin-cli reads the cookie from the data directory or uses -rpcuser/-rpcpassword; -stdinrpcpass avoids exposing a password in the process command line. ([documentation](https://bitcoincore.org/en/doc/31.0.0/))<br>`gui`: bitcoin-qt (Qt 6.8 in 31.x) with node, wallet and debug console; on Windows it stores GUI settings in HKCU\Software\Bitcoin\Bitcoin-Qt (network-specific variants such as Bitcoin-Qt-testnet4) and blocks Windows session end until it has shut down cleanly. ([documentation](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/doc/files.md))<br>`file`: bitcoin.conf (never written by the node), settings.json (read-write dynamic settings that override bitcoin.conf), debug.log, .cookie, bitcoind.pid and .lock in the data directory; wallets under wallets/<name>/wallet.dat (SQLite). ([documentation](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/doc/files.md))<br>`unix-socket`: Experimental Cap'n Proto IPC interface (mining interface used by Stratum v2 template providers) exposed by the multiprocess bitcoin-node binary via -ipcbind=unix (30.0+). Not available on Windows: ENABLE_IPC is limited to non-WIN32 builds and depends sets NO_IPC=1 for mingw32, so Windows release ZIPs contain no bitcoin-node.exe or bitcoin-gui.exe. — authentication: Filesystem permissions on the socket path. ([documentation](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/doc/multiprocess.md)) |
| Command-line interface | Windows ZIP bin\: bitcoin.exe (wrapper), bitcoind.exe, bitcoin-qt.exe, bitcoin-cli.exe, bitcoin-wallet.exe, bitcoin-tx.exe, bitcoin-util.exe; libexec\test_bitcoin.exe. The NSIS installer puts bitcoin-qt.exe and bitcoin.exe in the install root and bitcoind.exe, bitcoin-cli.exe, bitcoin-tx.exe, bitcoin-wallet.exe and test_bitcoin.exe in a daemon\ subfolder (no bitcoin-util.exe). Notable flags: -datadir, -conf, -chain=main\|test\|testnet4\|signet\|regtest, -testnet4, -signet, -signetchallenge, -regtest, -prune, -txindex, -blockfilterindex, -dbcache, -reindex, -reindex-chainstate, -server, -rest, -rpcauth, -rpcbind/-rpcallowip, -zmqpub*, -proxy, -onion, -i2psam, -listen, -natpmp, -printtoconsole, -help, -help-debug. -daemon is rejected on Windows ('-daemon is not supported on this operating system'). bitcoin-cli: -named, -rpcwait, -rpcwaittimeout, -rpcclienttimeout (default 900 s), -rpcwallet, -getinfo, -netinfo, -addrinfo, -stdin, -stdinrpcpass. |
| Remote management | No built-in remote administration or TLS. Remote control is JSON-RPC through a secured channel (SSH local port forwarding, WireGuard or Tailscale, or an authenticated Tor onion service) with rpcauth credentials, optionally restricted by rpcwhitelist; -rpcbind is ignored unless -rpcallowip is also set, and 32.0 disconnects disallowed clients immediately. REST and ZMQ are unauthenticated. Upstream explicitly says not to enable RPC connections over the public internet. A Linux node can additionally be managed over SSH (systemd units are shipped in contrib/init). |
| Node compatibility | Reference implementation for the SHA256d Bitcoin chain followed by most of the ecosystem. Downstream software typically needs server=1, cookie or rpcauth credentials and, depending on the consumer, txindex=1 (incompatible with pruning), blockfilterindex=basic, or ZMQ rawblock/rawtx/hashblock/sequence publishers. Version-aware behaviour matters: legacy (BDB) wallets and legacy-only RPCs were removed in 30.0, cluster mempool replaced ancestor/descendant limits in 31.0, and several RPC fields are deprecated behind -deprecatedrpc. Bitcoin Knots shares the network magic, ports, default data directory, default install directory and GUI registry key, but since 29.4.1.knots20260508 validates a hard-forked chain (BLAKE2b proof of work from height 961640) and is not consensus-compatible with Bitcoin Core. |
| Dependencies | optional: [Tor (C tor daemon, Tor Expert Bundle)](#entry-tor) — SOCKS5 proxy (-proxy or -onion, typically 127.0.0.1:9050; Tor Browser uses 9150) for onion peers, and the control port (-torcontrol, default 127.0.0.1:9051) for automatic ephemeral onion services (-listenonion=1 by default when listening). Version 3 onion services only.<br>optional: [i2pd (I2P daemon)](#entry-i2pd) or [I2P (Java I2P router)](#entry-i2p) — I2P via the SAM v3 bridge (-i2psam=<ip:port>; -i2pacceptincoming default 1). The 32.0 draft notes that legacy ElGamal I2P sessions will be removed on or before v34.<br>optional: [cjdns](#entry-cjdns) — CJDNS reachability flag (-cjdnsreachable). The 32.0 release-notes draft says the project is considering dropping CJDNS support.<br>optional: [HWI (Hardware Wallet Interface)](#entry-hwi) — External signer (-signer=<cmd>, enumeratesigners, walletdisplayaddress) for hardware wallets; support on Windows was re-enabled in 30.0.<br>optional: [Gpg4win](#entry-gpg4win) — Only for the manual verification procedure on bitcoincore.org; BTCortex should verify signatures natively instead of requiring GnuPG.<br>conflicts: [Bitcoin Knots](#entry-bitcoin-knots) — Same default data directory, default install directory (C:\Program Files\Bitcoin), P2P and RPC ports, bitcoin: URI handler and bitcoin-qt registry key. Knots 29.4.1.knots20260508 and later follow an incompatible chain; never let the two share a data directory or run with the same ports. |
| Networking | P2P listens on 0.0.0.0:8333 (mainnet) when -listen=1 (default unless -proxy, -connect or -maxconnections=0 is set); onion inbound bound to 127.0.0.1:8334. RPC and REST bind only to 127.0.0.1 and ::1 by default. Outbound: 8 full-relay and 2 block-relay-only peers plus short-lived feelers; -maxconnections default 125 (200 in 32.0, with -inboundrelaypercent=50). -natpmp=1 by default since 30.0 (PCP or NAT-PMP mapping on the router); UPnP was removed in 29.0/30.0. DNS seeds and hard-coded fixed seeds are used for bootstrap. Testnet3 18333/18332, testnet4 48333/48332, signet 38333/38332, regtest 18444/18443 (P2P/RPC). Running bitcoind with a non-loopback listener is expected to trigger a Windows Defender Firewall prompt on first run. |
| Storage | As of 2026-10-21: Bitcoin Core 31.1 chain parameters assume 856 GB of mainnet block data and 14 GB of chainstate (the figures used by the GUI's disk-space estimate, which include headroom); the download page still states 'about 600GB' plus 5-10 GB per month. Pruning (-prune=550 or more, in MiB) limits block and undo files only; the chainstate and block index remain. Other networks (31.1 estimates): testnet3 245 GB + 19 GB, testnet4 31 GB + 2 GB, signet 24 GB + 4 GB. Optional indexes (txindex, txospenderindex, coinstatsindex, blockfilterindex) add space; 32.0 halves the size of a rebuilt txindex. |
| Resources | -dbcache defaults to 1024 MiB when at least 4096 MiB of RAM is detected on 64-bit systems, otherwise 450 MiB (31.0+); a start-up warning appears when dbcache exceeds 75% of RAM. -maxmempool 300 MB, and unused mempool allowance is shared with the coins cache. -par 0 (automatic, up to 15 script-verification threads), -rpcthreads 16. Initial block download is CPU-, disk- and bandwidth-intensive; upstream gives no fixed RAM or CPU minimum. |
| Security implications | RPC is full control of the node and any loaded wallet (spending, chain manipulation, file writes on the host); keep it on loopback, prefer the cookie (protected by the data directory's NTFS ACL; -rpccookieperms maps only to POSIX-style bits) or rpcauth, never pass passwords on the command line, and use rpcwhitelist for scoped credentials. REST and ZMQ are unauthenticated. *notify and -signer options execute shell commands. Since 30.0 -natpmp=1 asks the router to forward the P2P port, which changes privacy exposure. Verify downloads with SHA256SUMS signed by multiple builder keys from bitcoin-core/guix.sigs; Windows executables are Authenticode-signed by 'Bitcoin Core Code Signing LLC' (DigiCert). Version warnings: <25.0 has High-severity remote crashes (CVE-2024-35202, CVE-2019-25220 <24.0.1); <29.0 is affected by CVE-2024-52911 (High, use-after-free in script validation); 30.0 and 30.1 were withdrawn because a failed legacy-wallet migration could delete wallet files; 31.0 with -privatebroadcast could leak the sender's IP (fixed in 31.1); 28.x is end of life since 2026-04-19 and 29.x becomes end of life with 32.0, after which three Medium/High issues fixed in 30.0 are due to be disclosed. |
| Licence | MIT |
| Licence notes | MIT licence; redistribution is permitted with the copyright notice, but BTCortex should download from bitcoincore.org and verify rather than bundle binaries. GitHub release pages carry no binaries and explicitly tell users not to use GitHub's links. No trademark policy was found on bitcoincore.org. |
| Integration mechanisms | Download the signed portable ZIP plus SHA256SUMS and SHA256SUMS.asc from https://bitcoincore.org/bin/bitcoin-core-<version>/ and verify natively: OpenPGP signature threshold over SHA256SUMS against pinned builder keys, then SHA-256 of the archive<br>Extract to a per-user, versioned runtime directory under %LOCALAPPDATA% (no administrator rights, no PATH or URI-handler registration) and check Authenticode signatures of the extracted executables as defence in depth<br>Create a dedicated data directory per node profile and always pass -datadir explicitly; generate bitcoin.conf with comment and unknown-key preservation; read settings.json to compute effective settings<br>Spawn and supervise bitcoind.exe as a child process (CREATE_NO_WINDOW, separated arguments, drained stdout and stderr), poll RPC until warm-up (-28) ends<br>JSON-RPC 2.0 client with cookie authentication, per-wallet endpoints, batch requests and version-aware method catalogue (help parsing; getopenrpcinfo from 32.0)<br>Graceful stop with the stop RPC, waiting for process exit and release of .lock; handle WM_QUERYENDSESSION in BTCortex to stop managed nodes before Windows logs off or shuts down<br>Tail debug.log with shared read access (getrpcinfo returns logpath) and toggle debug categories at runtime with the logging RPC<br>Subscribe to ZMQ publishers on loopback for event monitoring<br>Detect and import existing installations: registry (HKCU\SOFTWARE\Bitcoin Core, uninstall key, HKCU\Software\Bitcoin\Bitcoin-Qt strDataDir), C:\Program Files\Bitcoin, %APPDATA%\Bitcoin and %LOCALAPPDATA%\Bitcoin, running processes and .lock probing<br>Launch bitcoin-qt.exe as an external application on its own data directory<br>Manage remote nodes through SSH-tunnelled RPC with rpcauth credentials<br>Run the Linux build in WSL2 when IPC/multiprocess features (Stratum v2 template providers) are required |
| Feasible support levels | Fully Managed, Remote Managed, Connected Application, Managed via WSL2, External Launcher, Managed via Docker |
| Recommended support level | Fully Managed |
| Implementation feasibility | high — Official signed x64 Windows binaries, a portable ZIP that runs without elevation (manifest requestedExecutionLevel asInvoker), a documented configuration format and a stable JSON-RPC interface make full lifecycle management straightforward. Limitations on Windows: no ARM64 build, no IPC/multiprocess binaries, no native Windows service mode, -daemon unsupported, and console-close or logoff events give only seconds before the process is killed, so BTCortex must stop the node itself. |
| Priority | P0 |
| Implementation status | researched |
| In-app catalogue | Yes |
| Notes | 32.0 is in its release-candidate cycle (rc4 on 2026-10-12); its draft notes raise -maxconnections to 200, add getopenrpcinfo/rpc.discover, replace libevent with a custom HTTP server, default to PSBT version 2, deprecate -walletrbf and removeprunedfunds, and add -rpcmaxconnections, -inboundrelaypercent and -prevoutfetchthreads; re-verify when the final notes are published. 30.0 and 30.1 binaries were moved to /bin/insecure-wallet-deletion/. The Windows default data directory moved from %APPDATA%\Bitcoin to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Bitcoin in 28.0, but an existing %APPDATA%\Bitcoin is still used. Custom signets share the same signet/ subdirectory, so each custom signet needs its own data directory. Testnet3 is deprecated (since 28.0) but still supported in 31.1 and 32.0rc4. |

**Requires verification**

- The x64 Windows build running under emulation on Windows 11 ARM64 was not tested and is not documented upstream.
- Actual mainnet block-data and chainstate sizes on 2026-10-21 were not measured; only the 31.1 chain-parameter estimates (856 GB + 14 GB) and the download page figure (about 600 GB) were verified.
- Sizes of txindex, coinstatsindex and blockfilterindex on mainnet were not verified.
- That a non-loopback P2P listener triggers a Windows Defender Firewall prompt on first run is expected Windows behaviour but was not reproduced.
- That -rpccookieperms has no meaningful effect on Windows is inferred from the Microsoft CRT _chmod semantics (read-only attribute only); not tested.
- No trademark policy for the name 'Bitcoin Core' was found; absence was not exhaustively confirmed.
- The Authenticode subject 'Bitcoin Core Code Signing LLC' was verified for 31.1 only; continuity of the certificate across future releases is not guaranteed.
- 32.0 behaviour is taken from the release-notes draft and rc4 sources; final release notes may differ.

### Bitcoin Knots

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | Full-node implementations |
| Purpose | Derivative of Bitcoin Core maintained by Luke Dashjr with additional relay-policy (spam-filter) options, retained legacy wallet features, extra RPCs and GUI additions. Since 29.4.1.knots20260508 it also enforces consensus changes that Bitcoin Core does not: the BIP110 Reduced Data Temporary Softfork rules and a BLAKE2b proof-of-work hard fork. |

Still based on the Bitcoin Core 29.x code line (default branch 29.x-knots; no 30.x or 31.x Knots branch). Repository pushed 2026-09-21; not archived. |

'pgpverifiable' builds are not Authenticode-signed; integrity relies on the OpenPGP-signed SHA256SUMS. |

| APIs and interfaces | `json-rpc`: Bitcoin Core 29.x-compatible JSON-RPC on the same ports (8332 mainnet, 18332 testnet3, 48332 testnet4, 38332 signet, 18443 regtest). 29.4.2 has 172 public methods plus 21 hidden ones. Additions over Core 31.1 include getgeneralinfo, getrpcwhitelist, listmempooltransactions, listprunelocks, setprunelock, maxmempool, savefeeestimates, scriptthreadsinfo, setscriptthreadsenabled, setfeerate, settxfee, sweepprivkeys, dumpmasterprivkey and the legacy-wallet RPCs removed from Core in 30.0 (dumpprivkey, dumpwallet, importprivkey, importwallet, importaddress, importpubkey, importmulti, addmultisigaddress, newkeypool, sethdseed, upgradewallet, getunconfirmedbalance). Missing compared with Core 31.1: getmempoolcluster, getprivatebroadcastinfo, abortprivatebroadcast and, since 29.4.2, getdifficulty (replaced by a difficulty_blake2b field). — authentication: As Bitcoin Core: cookie, rpcauth, rpcuser/rpcpassword, rpcwhitelist; Knots adds -rpcauthfile and the getrpcwhitelist RPC. ([documentation](https://github.com/bitcoinknots/bitcoin/blob/v29.4.2.knots20260508/doc/JSON-RPC-interface.md))<br>`rest`: Bitcoin Core 29.x REST interface with Knots additions /rest/fee and /rest/mempool/transactions; no /rest/blockpart endpoint. — authentication: None. ([documentation](https://github.com/bitcoinknots/bitcoin/blob/v29.4.2.knots20260508/doc/REST-interface.md))<br>`zmq`: Bitcoin Core topics (hashblock, hashtx, rawblock, rawtx, sequence) plus Knots wallet topics hashwallettx and rawwallettx (-zmqpubhashwallettx, -zmqpubrawwallettx). — authentication: None. ([documentation](https://github.com/bitcoinknots/bitcoin/blob/v29.4.2.knots20260508/doc/zmq.md))<br>`p2p`: Same network magic and default ports as Bitcoin Core (8333 mainnet). From mainnet height 961640 (testnet4 150308) blocks use BLAKE2b proof of work; Knots 29.4.1+ prefers NODE_BLAKE2B peers and tolerates up to 8 extra outbound connections to peers on stale rules (-maxstaleoutbound). BIP324 v2 transport on by default. ([documentation](https://github.com/bitcoinknots/bitcoin/releases/tag/v29.4.1.knots20260508))<br>`cli`: bitcoind, bitcoin-qt, bitcoin-cli, bitcoin-tx, bitcoin-util and bitcoin-wallet (29.x base: no 'bitcoin' wrapper command). — authentication: As Bitcoin Core. ([documentation](https://github.com/bitcoinknots/bitcoin))<br>`gui`: bitcoin-qt (Qt 5.15.19 in 29.4) with Knots additions such as a sweep-private-key dialog and mempool statistics; uses the same QSettings location as Bitcoin Core (HKCU\Software\Bitcoin\Bitcoin-Qt) and writes several GUI-changed options (for example prune, addresstype, walletrbf, maxuploadtarget, peerbloomfilters, peerblockfilters) to bitcoin_rw.conf. ([documentation](https://bitcoinknots.org/))<br>`file`: Same data-directory layout as Bitcoin Core 29.x plus bitcoin_rw.conf (read-write configuration file, -confrw) in the network data directory; settings.json may contain consensusrules=rdts after the user consented to BIP110 in 29.3.knots20260508/29.4.knots20260508. ([documentation](https://github.com/bitcoinknots/bitcoin/blob/v29.4.2.knots20260508/doc/files.md)) |
| Command-line interface | Same executables and most flags as Bitcoin Core 29.x. Knots-specific options include -corepolicy, -rejecttokens, -rejectparasites, -datacarriercost, -datacarriersize (maximum and default 83), -acceptnonstddatacarrier, -permitbarepubkey, -permitbaredatacarrier, -permitbareanchor, -permitephemeral, -mempoolreplacement, -mempooltruc, -spkreuse, -maxscriptsize, -maxtxlegacysigops, -bytespersigopstrict, -minrelaycoinblocks, -minrelaymaturity, -dustdynamic, -subdustfeepenalty, -blockmaxsize, -blockprioritysize, -consensusrules, -confrw, -lowmem, -pruneduringinit, -maxstaleoutbound, -torexecute, -uaappend, -upnp, -rpcauthfile, -statsenable, -walletimplicitsegwit, -walletoldsigs, -signetblocktime and the debug-only -softwareexpiry and -v2onlyclearnet. |
| Remote management | As Bitcoin Core: JSON-RPC over a secured tunnel with rpcauth and rpcwhitelist (Knots adds -rpcauthfile and getrpcwhitelist). No built-in TLS or remote administration. |
| Node compatibility | RPC-compatible with Bitcoin Core 29.x for most methods, but not consensus-compatible with Bitcoin Core from 29.4.1.knots20260508 onwards: Knots validates a chain with BLAKE2b proof of work from mainnet height 961640 (first BLAKE2b block on 2026-08-30 according to the project's linked site), BIP110 rules, a temporary 800 000 weight-unit block limit and, from 29.4.2, a longer coinbase maturity, while using the same magic bytes and ports. 29.3.knots20260508 and 29.4.knots20260508 required explicit consent to enforce BIP110 and, once mandatory signalling began at height 961632 on 2026-08-08, split from Bitcoin Core-following nodes. 29.3.knots20260507 and earlier follow the same chain as Bitcoin Core. Services built for the Bitcoin Core chain (Electrum servers, Lightning implementations, explorers, wallets) will follow Knots' chain when connected to it; their compatibility with that chain is unverified. |
| Dependencies | optional: [Tor (C tor daemon, Tor Expert Bundle)](#entry-tor) — Same Tor integration as Bitcoin Core, plus -torexecute to spawn a tor process if none is running.<br>optional: [i2pd (I2P daemon)](#entry-i2pd) or [I2P (Java I2P router)](#entry-i2p) — I2P via SAM (-i2psam).<br>optional: [cjdns](#entry-cjdns) — -cjdnsreachable as in Bitcoin Core 29.x.<br>optional: [HWI (Hardware Wallet Interface)](#entry-hwi) — External signer support (-signer) as in Bitcoin Core 29.x.<br>optional: [DATUM Gateway](#entry-datum-gateway) — Knots' release notes direct miners on its chain to run their own DATUM Gateway, but DATUM Gateway's README (read on 2026-10-23) says Knots versions after 29.3.knots20260507 are no longer compatible with it and would earn no mining rewards; not needed for non-mining nodes.<br>conflicts: [Bitcoin Core](#entry-bitcoin-core) — Shares Bitcoin Core's default data directory (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Bitcoin or legacy %APPDATA%\Bitcoin), default install directory (C:\Program Files\Bitcoin), ports, bitcoin: URI handler and QSettings key, yet follows an incompatible chain since 29.4.1.knots20260508. Never share a data directory or install directory between them. |
| Networking | Same default ports and bind behaviour as Bitcoin Core 29.x (P2P 8333, RPC 8332 on loopback, onion 127.0.0.1:8334). -natpmp defaults to 1; -upnp is still available (default 0); -maxconnections default 125; v2 transport on by default. Peers are mixed with Bitcoin Core nodes on the same magic bytes; Knots 29.4.1+ prefers peers advertising NODE_BLAKE2B and caps automatic outbound connections to peers on stale rules (-maxstaleoutbound, default 8, maximum 10). |
| Storage | Knots 29.4.2 chain parameters assume 810 GB of mainnet block data and 14 GB of chainstate for its own chain, testnet4 11 GB + 1 GB, signet 9 GB + 1 GB and testnet3 200 GB + 19 GB (estimates, 2026-10-21). Pruning works as in Bitcoin Core (-prune=550 or more) with an additional -pruneduringinit option; the 29.4.2 notes warn that nodes pruned past 2026-09-21 may need a full re-sync when upgrading. |
| Resources | When -dbcache is not set, Knots 29.3.knots20260508+ picks a RAM-aware default between 100 MiB and 2 GiB; -lowmem flushes caches when available memory falls below a threshold; otherwise similar to Bitcoin Core 29.x. |
| Security implications | Windows binaries are not Authenticode-signed ('pgpverifiable'), so integrity rests on SHA256SUMS signed by builder keys from bitcoinknots/guix.sigs (3 to 7 signatures on recent releases, always including Luke Dashjr's key 1A3E761F19D2CC7785C5502EA291A2C45D0C504A). Consensus divergence from Bitcoin Core creates replay and chain-confusion risk: Knots wallets sign with a new 'hardfork' signature hash by default (-walletoldsigs=1 gives up replay protection), coins created before the split exist on both chains, and wallets or services connected to a Knots node see Knots' chain. Builds stop accepting new blocks after a built-in software-expiry date (about 2028-11-06 for 29.4.2) unless softwareexpiry=0 is set. Inherits Bitcoin Core 29.x code, so Core security fixes arrive only when Knots backports them; legacy BDB wallets remain loadable. |
| Licence | MIT |
| Licence notes | MIT licence (inherits Bitcoin Core's). Download from bitcoinknots.org or the GitHub release and verify; no Authenticode signature is available for redistribution checks. |
| Integration mechanisms | Download the pgpverifiable portable ZIP plus SHA256SUMS and SHA256SUMS.asc from https://bitcoinknots.org/files/<major>.x/<version>/ (or the GitHub release) and verify natively against pinned keys from bitcoinknots/guix.sigs<br>Extract to a per-user runtime directory separate from any Bitcoin Core runtime; never use the NSIS installer, whose default directory is the same as Bitcoin Core's<br>Create a dedicated data directory per Knots profile labelled with the chain it follows; refuse to reuse a data directory last used by Bitcoin Core or by a Knots version on different consensus rules<br>Spawn and supervise bitcoind.exe and talk JSON-RPC exactly as for Bitcoin Core, with capability detection from getnetworkinfo.subversion (/Satoshi:29.4.2/Knots:20260508/) and the presence of difficulty_blake2b<br>Generate bitcoin.conf and read both settings.json and bitcoin_rw.conf to compute effective settings<br>Monitor getblockchaininfo/getnetworkinfo warnings for the software-expiry warning and prompt for an update<br>Launch bitcoin-qt.exe as an external application<br>Manage remote Knots nodes over SSH-tunnelled RPC |
| Feasible support levels | Fully Managed, Remote Managed, Connected Application, Managed via WSL2, External Launcher, Managed via Docker |
| Recommended support level | Fully Managed |
| Implementation feasibility | medium — Packaging and lifecycle mirror Bitcoin Core 29.x (same ZIP layout, RPC and files), so the technical effort is low. The rating is lowered because Knots 29.4.1.knots20260508+ follows a different chain: BTCortex needs a distinct network identity for it, chain-aware dependency checks for every connected service, explicit informed consent before installation, and must never pre-wire Bitcoin Core-chain services to it silently. Binaries lack Authenticode signatures. |
| Priority | P1 |
| Implementation status | researched |
| In-app catalogue | Yes |
| Notes | Versioning: <Bitcoin Core base version>.knots<YYYYMMDD>; since 29.4 the base number no longer matches a Bitcoin Core release (Core never shipped 29.4.1 or 29.4.2) and three releases share the suffix 20260508. Timeline (from Knots release notes and linked sites): 29.3.knots20260508 (2026-05-09) added BIP110 enforcement behind a consent prompt or consensusrules=rdts, with 29.3.knots20260507 offered without it; mandatory BIP110 signalling began at height 961632 on 2026-08-08 and enforcing nodes split from the chain followed by Bitcoin Core and most hash rate; 29.4.1.knots20260508 (2026-09-02) added a BLAKE2b proof-of-work hard fork activating BIP110 rules at height 961640, removed the consent requirement, enabled rejecttokens by default and added an opt-in SIGHASH_UNIFIED replay-protected signature format; 29.4.2 (2026-09-21) added a 45-day coinbase-maturity soft fork and replaced getdifficulty. Knots' release notes describe the SHA256d chain as an 'altcoin' and miners who stayed on it as attackers; Bitcoin Core does not implement BIP110, whose BIP status is Closed after its unsuccessful activation attempt. Optech (2026-09-25) notes that a pruned Knots node that enforced BIP110 probably still holds the last common block, so replacing it with Bitcoin Core and running reconsiderblock on the first rejected block may avoid a full re-sync. The project said further changes are planned around mid-October 2026 and August 2027. |

**Requires verification**

- That Windows SmartScreen or Microsoft Defender warn about the unsigned Knots executables was not reproduced.
- How Bitcoin Core behaves when started on a data directory that Knots 29.4.1+ has synchronised (BLAKE2b blocks in the block index) was not tested; a full re-sync or -reindex is assumed to be necessary.
- The exact behaviour of Knots 29.4.x when started on a data directory last used by Bitcoin Core after the split was not tested beyond the release-note statements about recovery and re-sync prompts.
- Exact hash-rate distribution between the two chains after 2026-08-08 was not verified from primary data; both Knots' own pages and Optech state that most SHA256d mining power did not follow BIP110.
- Which exchanges, wallets and services support Knots' BLAKE2b chain was not verified.
- Whether the 'mid-October 2026' Knots update announced in the 29.4.2 notes has been published elsewhere (no newer tag existed on 2026-10-21).

The project describes the API as fully compatible with the original bitcoind/bitcoin-qt; it has no wallet methods. — authentication: rpcuser and rpcpass for full access; rpclimituser and rpclimitpass for a limited user. ([documentation](https://github.com/btcsuite/btcd/blob/master/docs/json_rpc_api.md))<br>`websocket`: Websocket endpoint wss://host:8334/ws (mainnet) for the same methods and for notifications. — authentication: The RPC credentials. ([documentation](https://github.com/btcsuite/btcd/blob/master/docs/json_rpc_api.md))<br>`p2p`: Bitcoin peer-to-peer protocol. ([documentation](https://github.com/btcsuite/btcd/blob/master/sample-btcd.conf))<br>`cli`: btcctl, the RPC command-line client. — authentication: The RPC credentials. |

### electrs (Electrum Rust Server)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | Electrum servers |
| Purpose | Efficient Electrum-protocol server in Rust for personal and small-scale use. It keeps a compact index (about 7 % of the block data) and fetches transactions from the local Bitcoin Core node on demand. Since 0.12.0 it is built on the bindex library and reads blocks through Bitcoin Core's REST interface. |
| Official website | — |
| Official repository | <https://github.com/romanz/electrs> |
| Maintenance status | active — v0.12.0 published 2026-09-13 (0.11.1 on 2026-02-22, 0.11.0 on 2025-11-17, 0.10.10 on 2025-07-19). Latest master commit 2026-10-17. Repository not archived. Cargo.toml version 0.12.0 depends on bindex 0.1.2 (bindex-rs v0.1.3 tagged 2026-09-28). |
| Superseded by | — |
| Latest verified stable release | 0.12.0 (2026-09-13) — <https://github.com/romanz/electrs/releases/tag/v0.12.0> |
| Verification date | 2026-10-21 |
| Native Windows | partial |
| Windows versions | — |
| Windows architectures | — |
| Windows distribution | No official binaries for any platform ('There are currently no official/stable binary packages'). Source build only (Rust 1.85 or later, libclang for rust-rocksdb). Windows-specific code exists: the ctrlc crate replaces signal-hook on Windows since 0.10.8 (PR #1123, December 2024, which also added a Windows CI build without the Prometheus metrics feature). The current CI workflow only builds on ubuntu-latest. |
| WSL2 | likely |
| Docker | community-image |
| Other platforms | Linux from source (Debian 13 and Ubuntu 25.04 documented; dynamic linking needs RocksDB 9.10.0), a beta Debian repository maintained by a contributor (deb.ln-ask.me), macOS and other Unix-like systems from source, documented ARM cross-compilation. The repository Dockerfile is 'provided for demonstration purposes'. Community image getumbrel/electrs (v0.12.0 tag pushed 2026-09-17). |
| APIs and interfaces | `electrum-protocol`: Electrum protocol 1.4 only: server.version returns ['electrs/0.12.0', '1.4']; protocol_min = protocol_max = 1.4 in server.features. Plain TCP only (no TLS, no WebSocket), default 127.0.0.1:50001 mainnet, 60001 testnet3, 40001 testnet4, 60401 regtest, 60601 signet. Supports blockchain.transaction.broadcast_package (0.11.0) and blockchain.scripthash.unsubscribe; blockchain.scripthash.get_mempool is not implemented; no peer discovery. — authentication: None. Binds to loopback by default; upstream recommends tunnelling for remote access and an nginx stream proxy or Tor for encryption. ([documentation](https://github.com/romanz/electrs/blob/master/doc/usage.md))<br>`http`: Prometheus metrics endpoint (default feature 'metrics'): 127.0.0.1:4224 mainnet, 14224 testnet3, 44224 testnet4, 24224 regtest, 34224 signet; for example index_height. A contributor stated in PR #1123 that the Prometheus feature does not work on Windows. — authentication: None. ([documentation](https://github.com/romanz/electrs/blob/master/doc/monitoring.md))<br>`cli`: electrs [--conf <toml>] [--conf-dir <dir>] [--skip-default-conf-files] --network bitcoin|testnet|testnet4|regtest|signet --db-dir <dir> --daemon-dir <dir> [--cookie-file <path>] [--daemon-rpc-addr host:port] [--electrum-rpc-addr host:port] [--monitoring-addr host:port] [--log-filters INFO] [--index-lookup-limit N] [--ignore-mempool] [--disable-electrum-rpc] [--sync-once] [--no-auto-reindex] [--version]. Every option also exists as an ELECTRS_<NAME> environment variable. — authentication: The auth=USER:PASSWORD option can only be set in a config file, for security; cookie_file is allowed on the command line. ([documentation](https://github.com/romanz/electrs/blob/master/doc/config.md))<br>`file`: TOML configuration loaded from /etc/electrs/config.toml, ~/.electrs/config.toml and ./electrs.toml (in that priority order), then environment variables, then arguments; --conf and --conf-dir override everything given before them. The db_dir must be empty or already owned by electrs. ([documentation](https://github.com/romanz/electrs/blob/master/doc/config.md)) |
| Command-line interface | electrs (no subcommands). Typical managed invocation: electrs --skip-default-conf-files --conf <path>\electrs.toml. Key options: network, db_dir, daemon_dir, cookie_file or auth, daemon_rpc_addr, electrum_rpc_addr, monitoring_addr, log_filters, db_parallelism (default 1), wait_duration_secs (10), jsonrpc_timeout_secs (15), index_lookup_limit (0 = unlimited), auto_reindex (default true), server_banner. Release builds: cargo build --locked --release (static RocksDB) or with system librocksdb 9.10.0. |
| Remote management | No admin API. Only the Electrum protocol and the Prometheus endpoint are exposed. Installations on node platforms or Linux hosts are managed through SSH/systemd or the platform; BTCortex can health-check them over the Electrum protocol and scrape metrics through a tunnel. |
| Node compatibility | 0.12.0 requires Bitcoin Core 31.0 or later with the REST interface enabled (-rest=1): bindex reads /rest/blockhashbyheight, /rest/headers, /rest/block, /rest/spenttxouts (added in Core 30.0) and /rest/blockpart (added in Core 31.0). JSON-RPC (server=1) is used with the cookie (default <daemon_dir>/.cookie, or cookie_file) or auth=USER:PASSWORD. Pruning must be disabled (-prune=0). txindex is 'allowed but unnecessary'. No ZMQ. Versions 0.9 to 0.11 fetched blocks over P2P instead (daemon_p2p_addr, default 127.0.0.1:8333), which needed a listening node. Bitcoin Knots releases based on Core 29 are not expected to provide the Core 31 REST endpoints, and upstream states that hard forks are not supported. |
| Dependencies | requires: [Bitcoin Core](#entry-bitcoin-core) — Core 31.0 or later, rest=1, server=1, prune=0. The REST interface is unauthenticated and shares the RPC listener.<br>optional: [Tor (C tor daemon, Tor Expert Bundle)](#entry-tor) — Onion service (HiddenServicePort 50001 127.0.0.1:50001) gives remote wallets an encrypted, authenticated-by-address path without a TLS proxy.<br>optional: [nginx (nginx/Windows)](#entry-nginx) or [Caddy](#entry-caddy) — TLS termination for SSL clients (upstream documents an nginx stream block on port 50002).<br>conflicts: [Fulcrum](#entry-fulcrum) or [ElectrumX](#entry-electrumx) — Same default client port 50001 and the same role. |
| Networking | Listens only on 127.0.0.1:50001 (Electrum) and 127.0.0.1:4224 (metrics) by default on mainnet. Connects to bitcoind RPC/REST at 127.0.0.1:8332 by default (18332 testnet3, 48332 testnet4, 38332 signet, 18443 regtest). No outbound internet connections of its own. Electrum clients must use plain TCP (host:50001:t) unless a TLS proxy or Tor is added. Under WSL2 NAT networking (the only mode on Windows 10), a Windows-hosted bitcoind must be reachable on the WSL virtual network, not on 127.0.0.1. |
| Storage | Usage guide for 0.12.0: index about 56 GB for about 802 GB of blocks/*.dat as of July 2026. The final database is about 7 % of the block files but may reach about 14 % just before the final compaction. Upgrading to 0.12.0 needs at least 120 GB free for the mandatory reindex. The block files must stay on disk (unpruned node). |
| Resources | Low CPU and memory use after the initial index. Initial index of mainnet about 2 hours on a 6-core CPU with 32 GB RAM and a 2 TB NVMe drive (July 2026, 0.12.0); about 18 hours on an ODROID-HC1 (8 cores at 2 GHz, 2 GB RAM, SSD). Large or popular addresses are slower because electrs reads the relevant transactions from bitcoind for each query (index_lookup_limit caps 'too popular' addresses). |
| Security implications | Optimised for personal or family use. SECURITY.md: 'Denial-of-Service attacks are excluded from the threat model - DO NOT share your electrs instance with untrusted users!'. No TLS of its own. 0.12.0 requires Bitcoin Core's REST interface, which is unauthenticated and served wherever the RPC listener is bound, so RPC/REST must stay on loopback (or a host-only WSL network) and never be exposed to the LAN. Upstream recommends cookie authentication. auto_reindex (default true) silently rebuilds an inconsistent or old-format database, which takes hours. Default daemon_dir is ~/.bitcoin even on Windows, so a wrong guess silently points at the wrong node; always pass daemon_dir and cookie_file. No GitHub security advisories published as of 2026-10-21. |
| Licence | MIT |
| Licence notes | MIT; redistribution of self-built binaries is allowed with the notice. RocksDB is statically linked by default (RocksDB is dual-licensed GPL-2.0 or Apache-2.0). |
| Integration mechanisms | Connect to electrs on node platforms (Umbrel, StartOS, RaspiBlitz, MiniBolt and others) or remote Linux hosts: health-check over the Electrum protocol and generate wallet connection settings<br>Provision a BTCortex-owned WSL2 distribution, install a pinned electrs build inside it and run it as a supervised process<br>Generate electrs.toml (network, db_dir, daemon_dir, daemon_rpc_addr, cookie_file or auth, electrum_rpc_addr, monitoring_addr, log_filters) and start with --skip-default-conf-files so no stray config files apply<br>Adjust bitcoin.conf: rest=1, prune=0; for WSL2 NAT mode also an rpcbind on the WSL virtual adapter and rpcallowip limited to the WSL subnet, with a dedicated rpcauth user<br>Health probe: server.version (expect 'electrs/<version>', '1.4'), blockchain.headers.subscribe height compared with getblockcount, and Prometheus index_height<br>Generate client settings: host:50001:t for local or tunnelled use, or an onion address through Tor<br>Research spike: a BTCortex-built x86_64-pc-windows-msvc binary without the metrics feature, built and signed in BTCortex CI |

| Recommended support level | Connected Application |
| Implementation feasibility | medium — Upstream targets Linux and ships no binaries. On Windows, BTCortex can either use WSL2 (on Windows 10 the NAT networking mode means bitcoind RPC and the unauthenticated REST endpoint must be reachable from the WSL virtual network) or build its own unsupported Windows binary. 0.12.0 needs Bitcoin Core 31 or later with REST and an unpruned node. Its index is much smaller than Fulcrum's (about 56 GB, without txindex, versus 166 GB or more plus a 66 GiB txindex), which makes it the better choice when a full node fits on a disk of about 1 TB. |
| Priority | P1 |
| Implementation status | researched |
| In-app catalogue | Yes |
| Notes | 0.12.0 is a breaking upgrade: it requires Core 31 or later, rest=1 and a full reindex (the 0.11.0 RocksDB change already forced one). On 2026-10-21 the Umbrel app store still shipped 0.11.1 ('0.11.1-patch.1'). Upstream recommends the Blockstream fork for public servers. Sparrow enables request batching for electrs 0.9.0 and later, based on the server.version string. The signet RPC default in config_specification.toml (18554) is stale; the code uses 38332. |

| Category | Electrum servers |
| Purpose | Lightweight single-user Electrum server that imports the user's master public keys and addresses as watch-only into a Bitcoin Core wallet instead of indexing the whole chain; it worked with pruned nodes, blocksonly and txindex=0. |

Issue #309 (opened 2025-05-18) asks whether Bitcoin Core 30's removal of legacy wallets ends EPS; it has no maintainer reply. PR #313 (2025-12-07) adding descriptor-wallet support is open, unreviewed and unmerged. |
| Superseded by | — |
| Latest verified stable release | 0.2.4 (2022-06-16) — <https://github.com/chris-belcher/electrum-personal-server/releases/tag/eps-v0.2.4> |

| Native Windows | yes |
| Windows versions | — |
| Windows architectures | — |
| Windows distribution | electrum-personal-server-windows-release-v0.2.4.zip with an OpenPGP signature (.asc) on the GitHub release; the README tells Windows users to drag config.ini onto the packaged executable. |
| WSL2 | likely |
| Docker | unknown |
| Other platforms | Python package for Linux and macOS (pip install from the source release). |
| APIs and interfaces | `electrum-protocol`: Electrum protocol 1.1 to 1.4 (SERVER_PROTOCOL_VERSION_MIN 1.1, MAX 1.4) over TLS on 127.0.0.1:50002 by default, one client connection at a time; no Lightning support. — authentication: IP whitelist (ip_whitelist); TLS with a bundled default certificate (certs/cert.crt), which upstream says must be replaced if the connection crosses the internet. ([documentation](https://github.com/chris-belcher/electrum-personal-server/blob/master/README.md))<br>`file`: config.ini with [master-public-keys], [bitcoin-rpc] (host, port, datadir, wallet_filename, poll intervals, initial_import_count, gap_limit), [electrum-server] (host, port, ip_whitelist, certfile, keyfile, broadcast_method tor-or-own-node, tor_host/port), [watch-only-addresses] and [logging]. ([documentation](https://github.com/chris-belcher/electrum-personal-server/blob/master/config.ini_sample)) |
| Command-line interface | electrum-personal-server <config.ini> [--version]; electrum-personal-server-rescan for historical rescans. |
| Remote management | — |
| Node compatibility | Incompatible with Bitcoin Core 30.0 and later, and therefore with the current 31.1. Its setup creates a legacy wallet (createwallet electrumpersonalserver true true "" false false true, that is descriptors=false), and deterministicwallet.py imports addresses with importmulti. Bitcoin Core 30.0 can no longer create or load BDB legacy wallets and removed the legacy-only RPCs importaddress, importmulti, importprivkey, importpubkey and others. Historically worked with Core 0.17 to 29.x, including pruned nodes. |
| Dependencies | requires: [Bitcoin Core](#entry-bitcoin-core) — Only versions before 30.0 (legacy wallet and importmulti); wallet enabled, server=1. |
| Networking | TLS on 127.0.0.1:50002 by default; optional transaction broadcast through Tor (127.0.0.1:9050). |
| Storage | Negligible: no chain index, only the watch-only wallet in Bitcoin Core. |
| Resources | Very low CPU and RAM (polls Bitcoin Core every 30 s when idle and every 1 s while a client is connected, by default). |
| Security implications | Ships a default TLS certificate whose private key is public, so connections can be decrypted unless the user generates their own. Single client at a time. The watch-only wallet reveals the user's addresses to anyone with RPC access to the node. Unmaintained since 2022. Its legacy-wallet design cannot work with supported Bitcoin Core versions. |
| Licence | MIT |
| Licence notes | MIT (setup.py); no LICENSE file was found at the repository root. |
| Integration mechanisms | Detect an existing installation and explain the incompatibility with Bitcoin Core 30 or later; offer Sparrow's direct Bitcoin Core connection (sparrow) or a full Electrum server instead |
| Feasible support levels | Unsupported |
| Recommended support level | Unsupported |
| Implementation feasibility | none — Verified incompatibility: EPS 0.2.4 relies on legacy wallets and importmulti, both removed in Bitcoin Core 30.0, and the descriptor-wallet PR is unmerged. Pinning Bitcoin Core 29.x (end of life when 32.0 ships) only to keep EPS working is not acceptable. |
| Priority | P3 |
| Implementation status | researched |
| In-app catalogue | Yes |
| Notes | EPS was the classic answer for 'Electrum server on a pruned node'. For BTCortex's pruned test machine, the replacement is Sparrow connecting directly to Bitcoin Core (Sparrow's Cormorant layer creates a descriptor watch-only wallet; see the sparrow entry). Revisit EPS only if PR #313 is merged and released. |

| Other platforms | Unix-like systems ('should run on any flavour of unix'; tested on macOS and DragonFlyBSD). Python 3.10 or later (PyPI package e-x), database engine LevelDB (plyvel) or RocksDB (rocksdb-ng); experimental free-threaded CPython (for example 3.14t). Example Dockerfiles in contrib/; community image lukechilds/electrumx (latest tag v1.18.0, 2025-08-24, not yet 2.0). |
| APIs and interfaces | `electrum-protocol`: Electrum protocol 1.4 to 1.7 (2.0.0 added 1.7: blockchain.scriptpubkey.*, blockchain.outpoint.subscribe/get_status/unsubscribe, blockchain.transaction.testmempoolaccept, mempool.recent). Transports are declared in SERVICES as tcp://, ssl://, ws://, wss:// (example tcp://:50001,ssl://:50002,wss://:50004). No incoming connections are served until the server has caught up. 1.18.0 added traffic-analysis countermeasures (padding, small delays). — authentication: None at protocol level; TLS with SSL_CERTFILE and SSL_KEYFILE (self-signed is fine; Electrum pins it on first use). Session resource limits (COST_SOFT_LIMIT, COST_HARD_LIMIT, MAX_SESSIONS). ([documentation](https://github.com/spesmilo/electrumx/blob/master/docs/environment.rst))<br>`json-rpc`: LocalRPC (service rpc://, default localhost:8000) used by electrumx_rpc: add_peer, daemon_url, disconnect, getinfo, groups, log, peers, query, reorg, sessions, stop, plus inspect_session (2.0.0). — authentication: None; bind to localhost only. ([documentation](https://github.com/spesmilo/electrumx/blob/master/docs/rpc-interface.rst))<br>`cli`: electrumx_server (configured entirely through environment variables) and electrumx_rpc [-p PORT] <command>. ([documentation](https://github.com/spesmilo/electrumx/blob/master/docs/HOWTO.rst)) |
| Command-line interface | electrumx_server with environment variables COIN=Bitcoin, NET (mainnet, testnet, testnet4, signet, regtest; mutinynet coin added in 1.20.0), DB_DIRECTORY, DB_ENGINE (mandatory in 2.0: leveldb or rocksdb), DAEMON_URL=http://user:pass@host:port/ (comma-separated failover list), SERVICES, REPORT_SERVICES, SSL_CERTFILE, SSL_KEYFILE, CACHE_MB (default 1200), PEER_DISCOVERY (on\|off\|self, default on), PEER_ANNOUNCE, TOR_PROXY_HOST/PORT, MAX_SESSIONS, LOG_LEVEL. electrumx_rpc getinfo\|sessions\|peers\|stop ... |
| Remote management | LocalRPC on localhost only (tunnel for remote hosts). On Linux it is normally supervised by systemd, daemontools or runit; remote installations are managed over SSH. |
| Node compatibility | 2.0.0 for COIN=Bitcoin requires Bitcoin Core 31.0 or later (MIN_REQUIRED_DAEMON_VERSION) with txindex=1 and txospenderindex=1 (REQUIRED_DAEMON_INDEXES, checked with getindexinfo), and a non-pruning node. 1.19.0 to 1.20.0 required Bitcoin Core 28.0 ('or Knots 28') with txindex. RPC authentication only via user:password in DAEMON_URL (no cookie-file support found in the docs or daemon code), so BTCortex must create an rpcauth user. Knots compatibility statements predate the Knots 29.4.1 hard fork, and Knots 29.x lacks txospenderindex, so ElectrumX 2.0 cannot run on it. |
| Dependencies | requires: [Bitcoin Core](#entry-bitcoin-core) — Core 31.0 or later, txindex=1, txospenderindex=1, unpruned; rpcauth credentials.<br>optional: [Tor (C tor daemon, Tor Expert Bundle)](#entry-tor) — Onion service for clients; TOR_PROXY_HOST/PORT (autodetects 9050, 9150, 1080) for onion peers; FORCE_PROXY to route peer discovery through Tor.<br>conflicts: [Fulcrum](#entry-fulcrum) or [electrs (Electrum Rust Server)](#entry-electrs) — Same conventional ports 50001/50002 and the same role. |
| Networking | Nothing listens unless SERVICES is set; with SERVICES, an omitted host means all interfaces (except rpc://, which defaults to localhost:8000), so BTCortex must specify 127.0.0.1. Peer discovery is on by default and contacts other public servers over the clear internet, and the server announces itself unless PEER_ANNOUNCE is empty; set PEER_DISCOVERY=self (or off) for a private server. Outbound to bitcoind RPC (DAEMON_URL). |
| Storage | 2.0.0 changelog, measured on Bitcoin mainnet around height 950 000 (July 2026): ElectrumX DB about 122 GiB with LevelDB (about 106 GiB with RocksDB 9), plus .bitcoin/blocks 788 GiB, chainstate 12 GiB, indexes/txindex 66 GiB and indexes/txospenderindex 88 GiB (new in Core 31). 2.0 changed the on-disk schema: the old database must be deleted and the index rebuilt from genesis (no migration path). Switching between LevelDB and RocksDB also requires a full resync. |
| Resources | With the GIL, initial sync uses about 2 GB RAM; with free-threaded Python about 8 GB, but it takes a bit under half the time on a modern multi-core machine (2.0.0 changelog). RocksDB is about 25 % faster than LevelDB on an SSD. CACHE_MB defaults to 1200 (not recommended above 2000). Needs a large open-file limit (about 1024 during sync, more when serving). A 2022 Sparrow benchmark on a Raspberry Pi 4 (ElectrumX 1.16) took about a week for the initial index. |
| Security implications | Public-server features (peer discovery and self-announcement) are enabled by default and leak the host's existence and IP unless disabled. LocalRPC is unauthenticated. 1.19.0 fixed a denial-of-service vector (new sessions refused after MAX_SESSIONS on Python 3.12+); 1.16.0 fixed a remote crash when peer discovery was enabled. The DAEMON_URL embeds the RPC password in an environment variable, so keep the process environment private and use a dedicated, whitelisted rpcauth user. No GitHub security advisories published as of 2026-10-21. |
| Licence | MIT |
| Licence notes | MIT (PyPI e-x licence expression MIT). Distributed on PyPI as 'e-x' because kyuupichan owns the 'electrumx' name there. |
| Integration mechanisms | Connect to existing ElectrumX servers (self-hosted on Linux or node platforms): Electrum-protocol health checks and wallet connection settings<br>Provision inside a BTCortex-managed WSL2 distribution with a pinned Python virtual environment (pip install e-x[rocksdb] at a pinned version) and generated environment variables<br>Run a container built from the upstream contrib Dockerfile (no official image)<br>Use electrumx_rpc getinfo or the LocalRPC JSON-RPC port for status; stop with the LocalRPC 'stop' command |
| Feasible support levels | Connected Application, Managed via WSL2, Managed via Docker, Remote Managed |
| Recommended support level | Connected Application |
| Implementation feasibility | medium — Well documented and actively maintained, but not supported on Windows, configured only through environment variables, without cookie authentication, and from 2.0 it needs Core 31 or later with txindex and txospenderindex (about 154 GiB of extra node indexes on top of its own 106-122 GiB database). On Windows desktops, Fulcrum or electrs are better local choices; ElectrumX matters mainly as a remote or public server that BTCortex connects to. |
| Priority | P2 |
| Implementation status | researched |
| In-app catalogue | Yes |
| Notes | Version history worth surfacing in compatibility diagnostics: 1.17.0 dropped COIN=BitcoinSegwit and added signet and testnet4; 1.19.0 added protocol 1.6 and made rejecting unknown clients mandatory (DROP_CLIENT_UNKNOWN removed); 2.0.0 added protocol 1.7, a new database schema and mandatory DB_ENGINE. |

| Other platforms | Linux x86_64 (built on Ubuntu 18.04) and arm64 tarballs with Qt, OpenSSL, libzmq and jemalloc statically linked (they still need the system bzip2 library and a compatible glibc); Docker image cculianu/fulcrum for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64; macOS from source only ('Binary builds for macOS coming soon'); BSDs from source. |
| APIs and interfaces | `electrum-protocol`: Electrum protocol versions 1.4 to 1.6 (MinProtocolVersion 1.4.0, MaxProtocolVersion 1.6.0 in src/ServerMisc.h), as newline-delimited JSON-RPC over TCP (tcp=), TLS (ssl=), WebSocket (ws=) and secure WebSocket (wss=). Conventional mainnet ports 50001 TCP, 50002 SSL, 50003 WS, 50004 WSS (testnet 60001-60004). Client ports are only bound once the initial synchronisation has finished; before that connections are refused. Extra methods include blockchain.scripthash.get_status and blockchain.address.get_status (2.1.1). — authentication: None at protocol level. TLS with PEM certificate and private key (cert=, key=; optional separate wss_cert/wss_key for CA-signed WebSocket certificates). Per-IP limits (max_clients_per_ip 12, max_subs_per_ip 75000) do not apply to 127.0.0.1/::1 by default. ([documentation](https://electrum-cash-protocol.readthedocs.io/en/latest/))<br>`json-rpc`: Admin RPC on admin= (a bare port means 127.0.0.1, for example 127.0.0.1:8000): newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over plain TCP, used by FulcrumAdmin. Methods match its sub-commands: addpeer, ban, banpeer, bitcoind_throttle, clients, getinfo, kick, listbanned, loglevel, maxbuffer, peers, query, rmpeer, simdjson, stop, unban, unbanpeer. The admin servers are started together with the client servers after the first 'up to date' state, so they are not available during initial sync. — authentication: None. Fulcrum logs a warning if the admin port is bound to a non-loopback interface. ([documentation](https://github.com/cculianu/Fulcrum/blob/master/README.md))<br>`http`: Stats HTTP server on stats= (for example 127.0.0.1:8080) serving /stats (JSON: Bitcoin daemon, storage, server manager, subscriptions, jemalloc and simdjson sections) and /debug. It is started during application start-up, before synchronisation, so it is the only machine-readable progress source during the initial index. — authentication: None. The example configuration says not to expose this port to the public. ([documentation](https://github.com/cculianu/Fulcrum/blob/master/doc/fulcrum-example-config.conf))<br>`zmq`: ZeroMQ subscriber (client side). Fulcrum asks bitcoind for its endpoints with getzmqnotifications and subscribes to hashblock, and to hashtx only when zmq_allow_hashtx=true. Without ZMQ it polls every polltime seconds (default 2.0). ([documentation](https://github.com/cculianu/Fulcrum/blob/master/doc/fulcrum-example-config.conf))<br>`cli`: Fulcrum.exe [options] [config]. The CLI overrides the configuration file. Passing _ENV_ as the config argument reads the options from environment variables. — authentication: RPC password via -p, the RPCPASSWORD environment variable or the config file; -K/--rpccookie for cookie authentication. ([documentation](https://github.com/cculianu/Fulcrum/blob/master/doc/unix-man-page.md))<br>`file`: Plain 'key = value' configuration file (doc/fulcrum-example-config.conf, doc/fulcrum-quick-config.conf) using native path separators (Windows example: datadir = D:\FulcrumData\mainnet). There is no default config path on Windows. Logs go to stdout/stderr; the syslog option has no effect on Windows. ([documentation](https://github.com/cculianu/Fulcrum/blob/master/doc/fulcrum-example-config.conf)) |
| Command-line interface | Fulcrum.exe <config> or flags: -D/--datadir, -b/--bitcoind host:port, -u/--rpcuser, -p/--rpcpassword, -K/--rpccookie <file>, --bitcoind-tls, -t/--tcp, -s/--ssl, -w/--ws, -W/--wss, -c/--cert, -k/--key, --wss-cert, --wss-key, -a/--admin, -z/--stats, -T/--polltime, --db_mem <MiB>, --db-upgrade (one-time 1.x to 2.x conversion), --compact-dbs, -C/--checkdb, --pidfile, --ts-format, --tls-disallow-deprecated, --upnp/--no-upnp, --bd-timeout, --bd-clients, --dump-sh, -d/--debug, -q/--quiet, -v/--version, -h/--help. FulcrumAdmin.exe -p <adminport> getinfo\|stop\|clients\|peers\|ban\|kick\|loglevel\|query ... |
| Remote management | Admin RPC and the /stats endpoint are plain TCP/HTTP without authentication or TLS, so remote management needs an SSH tunnel, WireGuard/Tailscale or similar private channel. On Linux hosts and node platforms the process is managed through SSH and systemd or the platform. The Docker image passes the data directory and certificate paths through its entrypoint. |
| Node compatibility | Bitcoin Core 0.17.0 or later; 28.0 or later recommended for full Electrum protocol 1.6 (for example the submitpackage-based broadcast_package). Requirements: txindex=1 (verified at start-up by fetching the first transaction after genesis; otherwise 'txindex verification failed'), RPC enabled, and an unpruned node ('The node must not be a pruning node'). RPC authentication with rpcuser/rpcpassword (or the RPCUSER/RPCPASSWORD environment variables) or rpccookie=<path to .cookie>. The cookie file is 're-parsed each time we (re)connect to bitcoind', which handles cookie rotation on node restart. bitcoind_tls for HTTPS RPC proxies. ZMQ is optional but recommended (zmqpubhashblock), and is discovered automatically through getzmqnotifications. Networks: main, test (testnet3), testnet4, signet and regtest. The README's statement that Bitcoin Knots 'is also known to work perfectly well' predates the Knots 29.4.1 hard fork; against a post-fork Knots node Fulcrum would index the Knots chain, not Bitcoin. |
| Dependencies | requires: [Bitcoin Core](#entry-bitcoin-core) — Unpruned node with txindex=1 and RPC. zmqpubhashblock recommended. Enabling txindex on an existing node starts a background index build; getindexinfo reports synced=false until it finishes. Keep rpcthreads above bitcoind_clients (default 3) plus the other RPC clients.<br>optional: [Tor (C tor daemon, Tor Expert Bundle)](#entry-tor) — Onion service for remote wallets (HiddenServicePort to 127.0.0.1:50001/50002) and tor_proxy (default 127.0.0.1:9050) for discovering .onion peers. tor_hostname and tor_*_port only matter when announcing to the public server network.<br>conflicts: [electrs (Electrum Rust Server)](#entry-electrs) or [ElectrumX](#entry-electrumx) — All three use the conventional ports 50001/50002 and the same client-facing role. Run only one Electrum server per port set and per wallet profile. |
| Networking | Listening defaults: the documented TCP default is 0.0.0.0:50001 (all interfaces), so BTCortex must set tcp = 127.0.0.1:50001 and ssl = 127.0.0.1:50002 explicitly. SSL, WS, WSS, admin and stats have no default and are disabled unless configured. Outbound: bitcoind RPC (default 127.0.0.1:8332) and its ZMQ endpoint. Peer discovery (peering, default true) connects to other public Electrum servers. From 2.1.0 'Good' peers are refreshed every 30 minutes instead of being held open. announce advertises the server when hostname is set. Disable both for a private server. UPnP is off by default (upnp=true asks the router to forward the listening ports). A non-loopback bind is expected to trigger a Windows Defender Firewall prompt. |
| Storage | Mainnet index (Fulcrum datadir): the README says about 133 GB for BTC as of August 2023. A user reported a Fulcrum 2.0 datadir of 166 GB on 2025-10-14 (GitHub issue #304; scripthash_history 86 GB, txhash2txnum 23 GB, utxoset 14 GB, scripthash_unspent 6.4 GB). It also needs txindex in Bitcoin Core: the ElectrumX 2.0 changelog measured .bitcoin/indexes/txindex at 66 GiB and blocks at 788 GiB around height 950 000 (July 2026). The 1.x to 2.x --db-upgrade needed about 14.7 GB to 24 GB of extra free space in that report. The testnet datadir comment says about 8 GB (undated). SSD strongly recommended. |
| Resources | README minimum: 1 GB RAM and a 64-bit CPU. db_mem defaults to 2048 MiB or 25 % of physical RAM, whichever is smaller (2.0 release notes and example config; the man page still says 1024). Other defaults: txhash_cache 128 MB, worker_threads = number of CPU cores, history_lookup_threads 8 (2.1.4), bitcoind_clients 3. Initial mainnet sync takes 'anywhere from 4 hours to 20+ hours' on an SSD depending on hardware, and 'days' on an HDD (README, undated). A larger temporary db_mem speeds up the initial sync. Fulcrum 2.x databases survive crashes and power loss: at most the last few blocks are rolled back and re-synchronised. |
| Security implications | The server learns every address its clients query, so only a self-hosted server preserves wallet privacy. Admin RPC and /stats are unauthenticated and must stay on loopback. The 0.0.0.0 default TCP bind would expose the server to the LAN unless BTCortex writes loopback binds. Disable peering and announce on private servers to avoid outbound connections and advertising the host. TLS: RSA keys are fully supported, EC/DH/DSA keys are 'experimental'. Certificates can be replaced without a restart (SSLCertMonitor). Release verification: SHA-256 checksums in Fulcrum-<version>-shasums.txt, signed by Calin Culianu's DSA-2048 OpenPGP key D465 135F 97D0 047E 18E9 9DC3 2181 0A54 2031 C02C (signature verified for 2.1.4 on 2026-10-21; key published in Electron-Cash/keys-n-hashes). Antivirus heuristics have flagged FulcrumAdmin.exe (PyInstaller one-file) as a false positive (issue #203), so BTCortex should talk to the admin port directly rather than launch FulcrumAdmin.exe. Prefer cookie authentication to bitcoind. No GitHub security advisories published as of 2026-10-21. Use 2.1.1 or later on Windows: it fixes spammy Win32 API handle exhaustion messages with BTC (issue #324). |
| Licence | GPL-3.0-or-later |
| Licence notes | GPLv3 or later (LICENSE.txt and source headers). If BTCortex redistributes the binaries it must also offer the corresponding source. Downloading the official ZIP from the GitHub release at install time avoids bundling. No trademark policy for the Fulcrum name was found. |
| Integration mechanisms | Download Fulcrum-<version>-win64.zip plus Fulcrum-<version>-shasums.txt and .asc from the GitHub release; verify the OpenPGP signature against the pinned key fingerprint D465135F97D0047E18E99DC321810A542031C02C, then the SHA-256 of the ZIP<br>Extract to a per-user versioned directory under %LOCALAPPDATA% (portable, no administrator rights, no installer or registry entries)<br>Generate fulcrum.conf: datadir on the selected volume, bitcoind=127.0.0.1:8332, rpccookie=<Core network data directory>\.cookie, tcp=127.0.0.1:50001, ssl=127.0.0.1:50002, cert/key, peering=false, announce=false, admin=127.0.0.1:<port>, stats=127.0.0.1:<port>, db_mem sized to available RAM<br>Generate and keep a long-lived self-signed RSA certificate and key (PEM) for the SSL/WSS ports, and record its SHA-256 fingerprint for client pinning<br>Adjust the managed node's bitcoin.conf: txindex=1, zmqpubhashblock=tcp://127.0.0.1:<port>, prune=0; restart the node and wait for getindexinfo txindex synced=true<br>Spawn Fulcrum.exe <conf> as a supervised child process; capture and rotate stdout/stderr; poll /stats during initial sync and admin getinfo afterwards<br>Graceful stop through the admin RPC 'stop' once synchronised; during the initial sync rely on Fulcrum 2.x crash safety if no console control event can be delivered<br>Electrum-protocol health probe: server.version, server.features (genesis_hash must match the node), blockchain.headers.subscribe height compared with bitcoind getblockcount<br>Generate client connection settings for Sparrow and Electrum (127.0.0.1:50002:s plus certificate file or SHA-256 fingerprint) and an optional Tor onion endpoint<br>Detect existing installations by process name (Fulcrum.exe), listening ports and config files passed on the command line<br>Connect to Fulcrum on node platforms or remote hosts through an SSH tunnel, Tor or a private network (connected application)<br>Run the official cculianu/fulcrum image or the Linux tarball when the node itself runs in Docker or WSL2 |
| Feasible support levels | Fully Managed, Connected Application, Remote Managed, Managed via Docker, Managed via WSL2 |
| Recommended support level | Fully Managed |
| Implementation feasibility | high — Fulcrum is the only maintained Electrum server with official, statically linked x64 Windows binaries. The portable ZIP runs without elevation and uses a documented flat configuration file. Cookie authentication is re-read on reconnect. /stats is machine-readable during sync and the admin RPC is available afterwards. Hard requirements: an unpruned, txindex-enabled node, about 1 TB of disk for mainnet (blocks, txindex and the Fulcrum index), which rules out the 73 GB test machine. Windows caveats: logs only on stdout, graceful stop needs the admin port, and there is no Windows service mode. |
| Priority | P1 |
| Implementation status | researched |
| In-app catalogue | Yes |
| Notes | The 2.x database format (2.0, 2025) is not backward compatible. Upgrading a 1.x datadir requires the one-time, irreversible --db-upgrade, which must not be interrupted (signals are ignored during the conversion; it takes about an hour or more on BTC mainnet). --utxo-cache was removed in 2.0. The Docker entrypoint generates a self-signed RSA-2048 certificate valid for 365 days if none exists; the native Windows binary does not generate certificates. history_lookup_threads (2.1.4) speeds uncached history lookups 5 to 10 times. Open bug on 2026-10-18: issue #336 reports 2.1.3 silently stalling on macOS with Qt 5.15 (not the Windows build). |

**Requires verification**

- Whether Fulcrum.exe in the Windows ZIP carries an Authenticode signature was not checked.
- The Fulcrum 2.1.x mainnet index size on 2026-10-21 was not measured; 166 GB is a single user report from 2025-10-14, and the network (BTC mainnet) is inferred from the component sizes.
- Graceful shutdown of Fulcrum.exe on Windows through console control events (CTRL_C_EVENT mapped to SIGINT) when it is spawned without a visible console was not tested.
- OpenPGP.js (or the verifier BTCortex chooses) support for the DSA-2048 signature used on Fulcrum checksum files was not tested.
- Behaviour against a post-fork Bitcoin Knots node (29.4.1 or later) was not tested; that Electrum clients would reject its headers is inferred from Electrum's SHA256d proof-of-work check.
- The README's '4 hours to 20+ hours' mainnet sync figure is undated and was not measured on Windows hardware.

It is the backend of the Esplora explorer and blockstream.info, and supports Liquid/Elements. |

| Official repository | <https://github.com/Blockstream/electrs> |

| Windows versions | — |
| Windows architectures | — |
| Windows distribution | — |
| WSL2 | likely |
| Docker | official-image |

([documentation](https://github.com/Blockstream/esplora/blob/master/API.md))<br>`electrum-protocol`: Electrum protocol 1.4 (PROTOCOL_VERSION 1.4) on --electrum-rpc-addr, with response-size, write-timeout and global response budget limits; optional electrum-discovery feature (--electrum-hosts, --electrum-announce). — authentication: None. ([documentation](https://github.com/Blockstream/electrs/blob/new-index/README.md))<br>`http`: Prometheus metrics on --monitoring-addr: 127.0.0.1:4224 mainnet, 14224 testnet3, 44224 testnet4, 24224 regtest, 54224 signet. — authentication: None. ([documentation](https://github.com/Blockstream/electrs/blob/new-index/src/config.rs)) |
| Command-line interface | electrs (cargo run --release --bin electrs --) --daemon-dir <dir> [--blocks-dir <dir>] [--jsonrpc-import] [--cookie USER:PASSWORD] [--daemon-rpc-addr] [--network mainnet\|testnet3\|testnet4\|signet\|regtest\|liquid...] [--db-dir] [--http-addr] [--electrum-rpc-addr] [--monitoring-addr] [--lightmode] [--address-search] [--index-unspendables] [--utxos-limit] [--electrum-txs-limit] [--zmq-addr] [--tor-proxy] [--cors]. |
| Remote management | No admin interface; HTTP API, Electrum protocol and Prometheus metrics only. |
| Node compatibility | Bitcoin Core without txindex ('no txindex needed'). By default it reads blk*.dat files directly from --daemon-dir/--blocks-dir, so it needs filesystem access to the node's block files; --jsonrpc-import fetches blocks over RPC instead (for remote or low-memory setups). It builds a full index of every block, so it needs an unpruned node. --cookie takes 'USER:PASSWORD' (default: read ~/.bitcoin/.cookie). Elements/Liquid with --features liquid. Its indexes are incompatible with romanz/electrs. |
| Dependencies | requires: [Bitcoin Core](#entry-bitcoin-core) — Unpruned; local block files or --jsonrpc-import.<br>optional: [Elements](#entry-elements) — Liquid and Elements networks with the liquid feature. |
| Networking | HTTP API 127.0.0.1:3000 and metrics 127.0.0.1:4224 by default (mainnet); the Electrum port is set with --electrum-rpc-addr (the Esplora image exposes 50001). Outbound only to bitcoind (RPC, optional ZMQ) and, optionally, Tor for discovery. |
| Storage | README: the indexes needed 610 GB after compaction as of June 2020, with about double that free during compaction; --lightmode cuts roughly 50 % by querying raw transactions and block metadata from bitcoind on demand. No current figure is published; mempool's fork reported 1.3 TB in October 2023. |
| Resources | Indexing takes 'a few hours on a beefy machine with SSD' (README, undated); a high open-file limit is required. RAM needs not documented. |
| Security implications | Designed for public, high-load use (Blockstream recommends it over romanz/electrs for public servers). The HTTP API is unauthenticated; enable CORS only for known origins. --address-search entries are not removed after reorgs (best effort). Needs read access to the node's block files. |
| Licence | MIT |
| Licence notes | — |
| Integration mechanisms | Run as part of the official blockstream/esplora Docker image<br>Consume its Esplora HTTP API from BTCortex's native explorer when an instance exists locally or remotely<br>Use as the 'esplora' backend of mempool (MEMPOOL_BACKEND=esplora) |
| Feasible support levels | Connected Application, Managed via Docker, Remote Managed |
| Recommended support level | Connected Application |
| Implementation feasibility | low — Huge index (hundreds of GB to more than 1 TB), no releases, no Windows support and direct block-file access. Only sensible on large Linux servers; BTCortex should consume its API rather than manage it on a Windows desktop. |
| Priority | P3 |
| Implementation status | researched |
| In-app catalogue | Yes |
| Notes | The old 2018 GitHub releases must not be presented as current versions; BTCortex should track the commit or Docker image digest instead. |

([documentation](https://github.com/sparrowwallet/frigate)) |

| Resources | Indexing uses about 4 GB RAM for the default scriptPubKey cache (cacheSize 10M); DuckDB defaults to 80 % of system RAM; 16 GB is 'a comfortable baseline' and 8 GB works with a reduced cache and memoryLimit. Optional GPU (CUDA, Metal, OpenCL). |
| Security implications | Server-side scanning means the server receives the wallet's scan private key (kept only in RAM); this is acceptable for a self-hosted instance but a public Frigate learns which payments belong to the user, so BTCortex should only connect wallets to the user's own instance. Releases are signed with a known key. |

| Licence notes | — |

| Recommended support level | Fully Managed |

| Priority | P3 |
| Implementation status | researched |
| In-app catalogue | Yes |

The repository moved from dgarage/NBXplorer to btcpayserver/NBXplorer. Docker image nicolasdorier/nbxplorer:2.6.19 (linux/amd64, arm64, arm) pushed 2026-09-30. |

| APIs and interfaces | `rest`: REST API on 127.0.0.1:24444 by default (/v1/cryptos/btc/...): track derivation schemes, groups and standalone addresses, get unused addresses, balances, UTXOs and transactions, create PSBTs, broadcast, fee estimates (for example /v1/cryptos/btc/fees/3), rescans. — authentication: HTTP Basic with the credential in the .cookie file regenerated at every start (%APPDATA%\NBXplorer\<Network>\.cookie on Windows; reload after a 401). --noauth / NBXPLORER_NOAUTH=1 disables authentication and must only be used in isolated development environments. ([documentation](https://github.com/btcpayserver/NBXplorer/blob/master/docs/API.md))<br>`websocket`: Event stream over WebSockets, in addition to polling and long polling of the events endpoint. — authentication: Same cookie credential. ([documentation](https://github.com/btcpayserver/NBXplorer/blob/master/docs/API.md))<br>`library-api`: Official .NET client NBXplorer.Client (NuGet); community Node.js client NBXplorer.NodeJS (not maintained by the project). ([documentation](https://github.com/btcpayserver/NBXplorer/blob/master/docs/API.md))<br>`file`: settings.config ('key=value', for example chains=btc, btc.rpc.url, btc.rpc.user, btc.rpc.password, btc.node.endpoint, postgres=<Npgsql connection string>); every setting also exists as a command-line flag and an NBXPLORER_ environment variable.
