### LND

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | Lightning implementations |
| Purpose | Lightning Labs’ Lightning Network node, written in Go: channels, payments, routing and an on-chain wallet, with Bitcoin Core (bitcoind), btcd or Neutrino as its chain backend. It exposes gRPC and REST interfaces authenticated with macaroons, and is the base of Lightning Terminal, Loop and Pool. |
| Official website | <https://lightning.engineering/> |
| Official repository | <https://github.com/lightningnetwork/lnd> |
| Maintenance status | active — v0.21.4-beta and v0.20.5-beta published on 2026-10-01 (two maintained lines); release candidates v0.21.5-beta.rc1 and v0.20.6-beta.rc1 on 2026-10-22; repository pushed on 2026-10-23 and not archived. |
| Superseded by | — |
| Latest verified stable release | 0.21.4-beta (2026-10-01) — <https://github.com/lightningnetwork/lnd/releases/tag/v0.21.4-beta> |
| Verification date | 2026-10-23 |
| Native Windows | yes |
| Windows versions | Not stated by the project. Verified on Windows 10 22H2 (19045) x64 on 2026-10-23. |
| Windows architectures | x64, x86, arm64 |
| Windows distribution | One ZIP per architecture: lnd-windows-amd64-v0.21.4-beta.zip (49 391 174 bytes), lnd-windows-386 and lnd-windows-arm64, each holding lnd.exe and lncli.exe in a folder of the same name. No installer and no Authenticode signature (both executables reported NotSigned on 2026-10-23). Hashes in manifest-v0.21.4-beta.txt, signed in separate binary OpenPGP files manifest-<signer>-v0.21.4-beta.sig, with OpenTimestamps proofs. |
| WSL2 | likely |
| Docker | official-image |
| Other platforms | Release archives for other platforms; reproducible builds with go1.27.1 (make release); Docker image lightninglabs/lnd with a /verify-install.sh script. |
| APIs and interfaces | `rest`: REST (grpc-gateway) on restlisten, default localhost:8080: JSON over HTTPS with LND’s self-signed tls.cert. 64-bit integers are strings and bytes are base64. Routes used by BTCortex: /v1/state (answers without a macaroon), /v1/getinfo, /v1/balance/blockchain, /v1/balance/channels, /v1/channels, /v1/channels/pending, /v1/peers, /v1/fees, POST /v1/switch (forwarding history), /v1/invoices, /v1/payments, /v1/graph/info, /v1/channels/backup and /v2/watchtower/client. Streaming calls such as POST /v2/router/send answer with newline-delimited JSON objects {"result": …}. — authentication: Macaroon, hex-encoded, in the Grpc-Metadata-macaroon header. Errors are grpc-gateway JSON {code, message, details}; observed on 0.21.4: "expected 1 macaroon, got 0", "verification failed: signature mismatch after caveat verification", "permission denied", "watchtower client not active". ([documentation](https://lightning.engineering/api-docs/api/lnd/))<br>`grpc`: gRPC on rpclisten, default localhost:10009, with the same certificate and macaroons; used by lncli, Lightning Terminal, Loop and Pool. Sub-servers (routerrpc, walletrpc, invoicesrpc, signrpc, chainrpc, peersrpc, watchtowerrpc and others) are included in release builds. — authentication: Macaroon in the macaroon metadata field, TLS with tls.cert. ([documentation](https://lightning.engineering/api-docs/api/lnd/))<br>`p2p`: Lightning peer protocol (BOLT 8 transport) on listen, default port 9735. — authentication: Node keys (Noise_XK). ([documentation](https://github.com/lightning/bolts/blob/master/08-transport.md))<br>`cli`: lncli.exe drives the gRPC interface. — authentication: The same macaroons and certificate. |
| Command-line interface | lnd.exe takes go-flags options; on Windows lnd --help prints the /option:value form and --option=value is also accepted, but a switch takes no value on the command line (--noseedbackup=true is refused, verified on 0.21.4). Exactly one of bitcoin.mainnet, testnet, testnet4, signet, regtest or simnet is required. Settings can also go in lnd.conf, an INI file whose keys carry their namespace (bitcoin.mainnet=true under [Bitcoin]). |
| Remote management | REST and gRPC over TLS with macaroons are meant for remote use: tlsextraip and tlsextradomain add names to the certificate, node packages show lndconnect:// URIs for wallets, and tor.active publishes an onion service. A macaroon can be baked with fewer permissions and with caveats such as time-before. |
| Node compatibility | bitcoin.node=bitcoind needs Bitcoin Core with RPC and either ZMQ (zmqpubrawblock and zmqpubrawtx) or bitcoind.rpcpolling; btcd and Neutrino are the alternatives. Verified on 2026-10-23: LND 0.21.4-beta with Bitcoin Core 31.1 on regtest, using bitcoind.rpccookie and bitcoind.rpcpolling with 1 s polling intervals. |
| Dependencies | requires: [Bitcoin Core](#entry-bitcoin-core) — Or btcd, or Neutrino without a full node. With bitcoind: RPC credentials or the cookie, and ZMQ or RPC polling.<br>optional: [Tor (C tor daemon, Tor Expert Bundle)](#entry-tor) — tor.active for an onion service and for reaching onion peers. |
| Networking | Listens on 9735 for peers, 10009 for gRPC and 8080 for REST (the last two on localhost by default). Connects out to peers, the bitcoind RPC and ZMQ endpoints, and with Tor through its SOCKS port. |
| Storage | Under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Lnd: lnd.conf, tls.cert, tls.key, logs, and data\chain\bitcoin\<network>\ with wallet.db, the macaroons (admin, readonly, invoice) and channel.backup; the channel database and graph under data\graph\<network>\ (bbolt by default; SQLite and Postgres backends are compiled into release builds). Mainnet size not measured here. |
| Resources | Not measured on mainnet. On regtest each lnd 0.21.4 process reached synced_to_chain in about 5 s. |
| Security implications | admin.macaroon can spend; readonly.macaroon is enough for monitoring and can export the static channel backup. tls.cert is self-signed; LND creates a new one when it is deleted, and with tlsautorefresh when its addresses change, which breaks clients that pinned the old one. The wallet is encrypted with the password chosen at creation; the 24-word aezeed seed together with channel.backup recovers channel funds. --noseedbackup creates an unencrypted wallet without showing a seed (tests only). Releases: manifest-v<version>.txt must carry signatures from at least 5 of the 16 keys listed in scripts/verify-install.sh, each user counted once; v0.21.4-beta carried 8 valid signatures (bhandras, boris, georgetsagk, gijswijs, roasbeef, suheb, ViktorT-11, ziggie1984) on 2026-10-23. One listed key (ellemouton) expired on 2026-06-21. |
| Licence | MIT |
| Licence notes | MIT (LICENSE: Copyright (C) 2015-2022 Lightning Labs and The Lightning Network Developers). |
| Integration mechanisms | Connect over REST with the read-only macaroon (kept in the vault) and the certificate pinned by its SHA-256 fingerprint<br>Find LND on this computer in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Lnd and read lnd.conf (restlisten, norest, network, datadir, tlscertpath, *macaroonpath) without changing it<br>Accept lndconnect:// URIs from node packages; refuse the gRPC port 10009<br>Read what a macaroon allows from its identifier (entity and action pairs) without asking the node<br>Reach onion addresses through BTCortex’s tor with per-connection SOCKS stream isolation<br>Export the static channel backup through /v1/channels/backup and keep it in BTCortex’s backups folder<br>Install the Windows ZIP after checking 5 of the 16 release keys on the manifest (used for integration tests)<br>Run lnd as a managed process for a BTCortex node (not implemented: creating the wallet shows its seed, which must happen in LND’s own tools) |
| Feasible support levels | Connected Application, Remote Managed, Fully Managed, Managed via Docker |
| Recommended support level | Connected Application |
| Implementation feasibility | high — Official Windows builds, documented REST and gRPC, read-only macaroons, and an end-to-end test of BTCortex against three LND 0.21.4 nodes on Windows 10 regtest (payments routed through a middle node, forwarding fees, channel backup verified by LND). |
| Priority | P0 |
| Implementation status | integration-tested |
| In-app catalogue | Yes |
| Notes | go-flags option syntax and lnd.conf layout were checked against lnd 0.21.4 on Windows. The REST interface reports peer aliases on channels with peer_alias_lookup=true. Gossip of channel policies takes a moment after channels are announced: route queries (/v1/graph/routes) fail until both policies are known. |

Release builds are Win32 tray applications. 2.61.0 has SHA512SUMS and SHA512SUMS.asc (issuer 9519 28BB 3170 24EF D053 D73C 66F6 C87B 98EB CFE2, R4SAS); the 3.0.0 release had no SHA512SUMS or signature on 2026-10-21. |

| APIs and interfaces | `other`: SAM application bridge (sam.enabled true by default, usually 127.0.0.1:7656; SAM UDP 7655). Bitcoin Core speaks SAM 3.1 to it. — authentication: None (bind to loopback) ([documentation](https://i2p.net/en/docs/api/samv3/))<br>`http`: Web console (http.enabled true, port 7070) and HTTP proxy (httpproxy, port 4444); both enabled by default. — authentication: Optional HTTP basic authentication for the web console ([documentation](https://github.com/PurpleI2P/i2pd_docs_en/blob/master/docs/user-guide/configuration.md))<br>`socks`: SOCKS proxy into I2P (socksproxy, port 4447, enabled by default). ([documentation](https://github.com/PurpleI2P/i2pd_docs_en/blob/master/docs/user-guide/configuration.md))<br>`json-rpc`: I2PControl JSON-RPC over HTTPS (i2pcontrol.enabled false by default, port 7650): Authenticate, RouterInfo, RouterManager (Shutdown, ShutdownGraceful), plus the i2pd-specific LocalDestinationInfo. — authentication: Password (default 'itoopie', must be changed) exchanged for a session token; self-signed TLS certificate i2pcontrol.crt.pem ([documentation](https://github.com/PurpleI2P/i2pd_docs_en/blob/master/docs/devs/api/I2PControl.md))<br>`file`: i2pd.conf (INI) and tunnels.conf in the data directory; router keys, netDb and peer profiles. ([documentation](https://github.com/PurpleI2P/i2pd_docs_en/blob/master/docs/user-guide/configuration.md)) |
| Command-line interface | i2pd.exe --datadir=<dir> --conf=<dir>\i2pd.conf --tunconf=<dir>\tunnels.conf [--service] [--loglevel=warn]. datadir and service are command-line-only options. Without --datadir the data directory is the executable's folder if it contains i2pd.conf, otherwise %APPDATA%\i2pd; --service uses C:\ProgramData\i2pd. The 'daemon' option defaults to false in the source (Config.cpp) although the documentation table says true. |
| Remote management | I2PControl JSON-RPC (HTTPS, password) and the web console; both should stay on loopback. |
| Node compatibility | Bitcoin Core (22.0+): i2psam=127.0.0.1:7656, i2pacceptincoming=1 (default; a persistent I2P address with its key in i2p_private_key in the data directory) or 0 (transient address per outbound connection), onlynet=i2p optional. Core uses SAM 3.1, so it listens and advertises with port 0 and only connects to I2P addresses with port 0. Core's I2P documentation recommends i2pd as the lighter alternative. |
| Dependencies | None recorded |
| Networking | NTCP2 and SSU2 transports on a random port (port option, default 'auto') on all interfaces; UPnP is false by default for the command-line build but true for the GUI builds (Windows, Android). Participates in transit tunnels by default, which Core's documentation asks users not to restrict. Local listeners: 7070 web console, 4444 HTTP proxy, 4447 SOCKS proxy, 7656 SAM, 7654 I2CP (enabled by default), 7650 I2PControl (disabled by default). |
| Storage | Windows x64 ZIP 4.9 MB (3.0.0); netDb and profiles are small. |
| Resources | Bandwidth limit configurable (bandwidth L=32 KB/s, O=256 KB/s, P=2048 KB/s, X=unlimited; share percentage for transit); RAM and CPU not measured. |
| Security implications | Unlike Tor, the receiver of an I2P connection sees the initiator's I2P address (Core's i2p.md), so transient addresses (i2pacceptincoming=0) are preferable when inbound is not needed. Disable UPnP for BTCortex-managed routers (Windows GUI builds enable it by default) and bind every local service to 127.0.0.1. Change the default I2PControl password. A non-administrator user who sees the Windows Firewall prompt for i2pd's transport listener gets block rules whatever they choose; I2P still works outbound but is reachability-limited. Verify the 2.61.0-style SHA512SUMS.asc when present; for 3.0.0 no signature was published at the time of checking. |
| Licence | BSD-3-Clause |
| Licence notes | — |
| Integration mechanisms | Download the win64 ZIP, verify SHA512SUMS and its OpenPGP signature (R4SAS key), extract per user<br>Generate i2pd.conf (SAM on 127.0.0.1:7656, web console on 127.0.0.1 with authentication or disabled, HTTP and SOCKS proxies disabled unless needed, upnp disabled, I2PControl on 127.0.0.1 with a random password) and launch with --datadir and --conf<br>Health: SAM 'HELLO VERSION' handshake on 7656 and I2PControl RouterInfo; Bitcoin Core getnetworkinfo shows the i2p network as reachable<br>Stop through I2PControl RouterManager Shutdown (immediate) or ShutdownGraceful (finishes transit tunnels, up to about ten minutes)<br>Write bitcoin.conf i2psam and i2pacceptincoming settings |
| Feasible support levels | Fully Managed, Connected Application, Managed via WSL2 |
| Recommended support level | Fully Managed |
| Implementation feasibility | medium — Portable signed ZIP and simple INI configuration, but the Windows builds are tray applications, the newest release lacked checksums at the time of checking, UPnP is on by default in the GUI build, and the transport listener triggers a Windows Firewall prompt. |
| Priority | P2 |
| Implementation status | researched |
| In-app catalogue | Yes |
| Notes | I2P's SAM v3 specification page (updated 2026-07) says i2pd did not support most SAM 3.2/3.3 features; i2pd 3.0.0 (2026-10-20) announces a full SAM 3.3 implementation. Bitcoin Core only needs SAM 3.1. |

### Tor (C tor daemon, Tor Expert Bundle)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | Anonymity networks |
| Purpose | Reference C implementation of the Tor anonymity network (client, onion-service host and relay). On Windows the Tor Project ships it as the Tor Expert Bundle (tor.exe, pluggable transports, GeoIP data), which BTCortex runs per user as the SOCKS proxy and onion-service host for Bitcoin Core, Electrum servers, Lightning nodes and wallets. |
| Official website | <https://www.torproject.org/> |
| Official repository | <https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/core/tor> |
| Maintenance status | active — tor 0.4.9.14 was released on 2026-10-07 as a security release ('Another week, another security release'; fixes tracked as TROVE-2026-062 and TROVE-2026-067 among others). The 0.4.9 series became stable on 2026-02-12, 0.4.8 reached end of life on 2026-06-01 and the 0.5.0 merge window opened on 2026-03-25 (CoreTorReleases wiki). Tor Expert Bundle 15.0.25 (tor 0.4.9.14) was published on dist.torproject.org on 2026-10-12 together with Tor Browser 15.0.25. |
| Superseded by | — |
| Latest verified stable release | 0.4.9.14 (Tor Expert Bundle 15.0.25) (2026-10-07) — <https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/core/tor/-/raw/tor-0.4.9.14/ChangeLog> |
| Verification date | 2026-10-21 |
| Native Windows | yes |
| Windows versions | Not stated for the Expert Bundle. Tor Browser dropped Windows 7, 8 and 8.1 with Tor Browser 14 and the Tor Project recommends Windows 10 or 11. |
| Windows architectures | x64, x86 |
| Windows distribution | Tor Expert Bundle tar.gz archives without an installer: tor-expert-bundle-windows-x86_64-<Tor Browser version>.tar.gz and tor-expert-bundle-windows-i686-<version>.tar.gz, each with a detached OpenPGP signature (.asc) made with the Tor Browser Developers signing key, plus a signed sha256sums-signed-build.txt. tor.exe in 15.0.25 has no Authenticode signature (empty PE certificate table). No Windows ARM64 build. The Tor Project states that Tor Browser 16.0 drops 32-bit x86 platforms. |
| WSL2 | likely |
| Docker | unknown |
| Other platforms | Expert Bundles for Linux (x86_64, i686; aarch64 only in the 16.0 alpha), macOS (x86_64, aarch64) and Android; source tarball for Unix-like systems; distribution packages. |
| APIs and interfaces | `socks`: SOCKS4/4a/5 listener (SocksPort, default 9050; BTCortex binds 127.0.0.1 only). Separate SocksPort lines are isolated from each other by default, and IsolateSOCKSAuth (on by default) puts streams with different SOCKS5 username/password on different circuits, which Bitcoin Core's proxyrandomize uses. Tor's SOCKS extensions add RESOLVE/RESOLVE_PTR and extended onion-service error codes. — authentication: None (loopback only). SOCKS5 username/password is used for stream isolation, not access control. ([documentation](https://spec.torproject.org/socks-extensions.html))<br>`control-protocol`: Tor control protocol on ControlPort over TCP (ControlSocket Unix sockets are not available on Windows). Line-based with SMTP-style reply codes (250 OK, 514 authentication required, 515 bad authentication, 552 unrecognised entity, 650 asynchronous event). BTCortex uses PROTOCOLINFO, AUTHCHALLENGE, AUTHENTICATE, GETINFO (version, status/bootstrap-phase, status/circuit-established, status/enough-dir-info, network-liveness, net/listeners/socks, onions/current, status/version/current), SETEVENTS (STATUS_CLIENT, STATUS_GENERAL, HS_DESC, NETWORK_LIVENESS), ADD_ONION, DEL_ONION, SIGNAL (SHUTDOWN, HALT, NEWNYM, RELOAD) and TAKEOWNERSHIP. — authentication: SAFECOOKIE (HMAC-SHA256 challenge-response over the 32-byte control_auth_cookie; recommended), COOKIE (deprecated by the specification), HASHEDPASSWORD (HashedControlPassword) or NULL (must never be used). ([documentation](https://spec.torproject.org/control-spec/))<br>`cli`: tor.exe -f <torrc>, --defaults-torrc <file>, --verify-config, --dump-config short|full, --hash-password <password>, --version, --list-modules and --service install|remove|start|stop (administrator only). Any torrc option can also be given on the command line ('--SocksPort 9050' or 'SocksPort 9050'); a '+' prefix appends to and a '/' prefix removes options from the configuration file. ([documentation](https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/core/tor/-/raw/tor-0.4.9.14/doc/man/tor.1.txt))<br>`file`: torrc and a defaults file; DataDirectory (state, cached consensus and microdescriptors, lock, control_auth_cookie); one HiddenServiceDir per onion service containing hostname, hs_ed25519_secret_key, hs_ed25519_public_key and authorized_clients/*.auth; ClientOnionAuthDir containing <name>.auth_private files; log files. — authentication: NTFS permissions of the per-user directories ([documentation](https://spec.torproject.org/rend-spec/))<br>`http`: Optional MetricsPort answering HTTP GET /metrics in Prometheus format. MetricsPortPolicy must be set (reject-all by default). The manual warns that exposing metrics publicly endangers Tor users; keep it on loopback if it is enabled at all. — authentication: None; MetricsPortPolicy address filter only ([documentation](https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/core/tor/-/raw/tor-0.4.9.14/doc/man/tor.1.txt)) |
| Command-line interface | tor.exe -f <torrc> --defaults-torrc <defaults> __OwningControllerProcess <pid>; tor.exe --verify-config -f <torrc>; tor.exe --hash-password <password> (for HashedControlPassword); tor.exe --version. tor --service install [--options ...] creates the Windows service 'tor' (display name 'Tor Win32 Service', auto-start, account NT AUTHORITY\LocalService) and needs administrator rights, as do --service start\|stop\|remove. |
| Remote management | Only through the control protocol. The ControlPort grants full control (configuration, onion-service keys, shutdown) and must never leave loopback; tor instances on remote machines or node platforms can be monitored through an SSH tunnel to their ControlPort with that machine's own authentication. |
| Node compatibility | Bitcoin Core: proxy=127.0.0.1:9050 (or proxy=<addr>=tor / onion=<addr> for onion-only routing; DNS lookups only use the generic or IPv4/IPv6 proxy), torcontrol=127.0.0.1:9051 with SAFECOOKIE (Core reads COOKIEFILE from PROTOCOLINFO, so it must run as the same Windows user) or torpassword with HashedControlPassword; when listening, Core creates an ephemeral v3 onion service with ADD_ONION and stores its key in onion_v3_private_key; onlynet=onion (the alias 'tor' was removed in 31.0); privatebroadcast (31.0+, use 31.1 or later); 32.0 enables proof-of-work defences for its onion service. Fulcrum: tor_proxy (default 127.0.0.1:9050) for .onion peer discovery, tor_hostname and tor_*_port to announce an onion endpoint, inbound via HiddenServicePort. Sparrow: useProxy/proxyServer or its internal Tor. Electrum: proxy socks5:127.0.0.1:9050. Wasabi bundles its own tor on 37150/37151. |
| Dependencies | optional: [lyrebird (Tor pluggable transports)](#entry-lyrebird) — Pluggable transports (obfs4, Snowflake, WebTunnel, meek) for bridges; lyrebird.exe ships in the Expert Bundle.<br>optional: [Conjure pluggable transport (conjure-client)](#entry-conjure) — Experimental Conjure transport; conjure-client.exe ships in the Expert Bundle. |
| Networking | Outbound TCP to guard relays, fallback directories or bridges (any port). No inbound port is needed for client use or for onion services, which work behind NAT and firewalls. Local listeners: SocksPort 9050 and ControlPort 9051 by default (Tor Browser uses 9150/9151, Wasabi's bundled tor 37150/37151); BTCortex binds both to 127.0.0.1 and checks for conflicts first. DisableNetwork 1 allows a configured but offline start. Bootstrap requires a correct system clock (CLOCK_SKEW status event). |
| Storage | Expert Bundle 15.0.25 for Windows x86_64: 21 MB archive; tor.exe 10.2 MB, tor-gencert.exe 6.2 MB, lyrebird.exe 18.0 MB, conjure-client.exe 13.1 MB, geoip 9.8 MB and geoip6 16.6 MB extracted (measured from the archive listing on 2026-10-21). The DataDirectory caches the consensus and microdescriptors; its size was not measured. |
| Resources | No official RAM or CPU figures for a client; not measured on the test machine. |
| Security implications | Verify the archive's OpenPGP signature against the Tor Browser Developers key (primary fingerprint EF6E 286D DA85 EA2A 4BA7 DE68 4E2C 6E87 9329 8290; 15.0.25 was signed with subkey 022D A248 432D 2A0E 0F54 E65E 316C 1FAC D62D 07D9) and the SHA-256 in the signed sha256sums-signed-build.txt; Authenticode cannot be used because tor.exe is unsigned. Releases are frequent and often security-relevant (0.4.9.14 fixed several high-severity bugs), so the update channel matters. The ControlPort is equivalent to full control of tor and its onion-service keys; use SAFECOOKIE, keep the DataDirectory and cookie readable only by the user (HiddenServiceDirGroupReadable has no effect on Windows) and never expose SocksPort or ControlPort beyond loopback (the manual warns that a non-local SocksPort leaks traffic and creates an open proxy). hs_ed25519_secret_key is the onion identity and must be protected and backed up like a credential. Log at notice level or below (the manual warns that more verbose logs may provide sensitive information). Tor does not start from paths containing non-ASCII characters (issue #10416 open; the proposed fix MR !357 was closed unmerged). A Tor-only node is exposed to Sybil and eclipse risks on a smaller address set. |
| Licence | BSD-3-Clause |
| Licence notes | The Expert Bundle also contains libevent, OpenSSL, zlib, lyrebird and Conjure under their own licences (docs/*.txt in the archive). Redistribution of the unmodified bundle is permitted; 'Tor' and the onion logo are trademarks of The Tor Project, whose trademark guidelines were not reviewed here. |
| Integration mechanisms | Resolve the current stable version (download.torproject.org/tor/ or the Tor Browser downloads.json) and download the Expert Bundle for the machine's architecture from dist.torproject.org (archive.torproject.org/tor-package-archive as fallback)<br>Verify the detached .asc against a pinned Tor Browser Developers key with OpenPGP.js, cross-check the SHA-256 in the signed sha256sums-signed-build.txt, then extract with path validation to %LOCALAPPDATA%\BTCortex\runtimes\tor\<version><br>Generate torrc and an explicit defaults file; launch tor.exe as a per-user child process with __OwningControllerProcess, then TAKEOWNERSHIP over an authenticated control connection<br>Authenticate with SAFECOOKIE, subscribe to STATUS_CLIENT, STATUS_GENERAL, HS_DESC and NETWORK_LIVENESS events and track bootstrap through status/bootstrap-phase<br>Create onion services with HiddenServiceDir/HiddenServicePort or ADD_ONION (Detach, PoWDefensesEnabled) and display hostnames; monitor HS_DESC UPLOADED events<br>Write bitcoin.conf (proxy, torcontrol, onlynet), Fulcrum, Sparrow, Electrum and Lightning proxy settings that point at dedicated SocksPorts<br>Detect external tor installations (listening 9050/9051, 9150/9151, 37150/37151; tor.exe processes; Windows service 'tor') with PROTOCOLINFO probes only<br>Stop with SIGNAL SHUTDOWN and wait, falling back to SIGNAL HALT and then process termination |
| Feasible support levels | Fully Managed, Connected Application, Remote Managed, Managed via WSL2 |
| Recommended support level | Fully Managed |
| Implementation feasibility | high — Official signed Windows archive, no installer and no administrator rights, a complete documented control protocol and a reference launcher (Tor Browser's tor-launcher) to copy. Open work: non-ASCII profile paths, port conflicts with other tor instances, antivirus or application-control policies against unsigned executables in user-writable folders, and bridges for censored networks. |
| Priority | P1 |
| Implementation status | researched |
| In-app catalogue | Yes |
| Notes | The Expert Bundle version number follows Tor Browser (15.0.25 contains tor 0.4.9.14); its data/torrc-defaults is Tor Browser's file and refers to TorBrowser\Tor\PluggableTransports paths that do not exist in the bundle, so BTCortex must write its own ClientTransportPlugin lines. Arti (arti) is the long-term successor but cannot yet replace C tor for BTCortex (no official binaries, no control port, onion-service hosting still documented as experimental). Do not depend on Tor Browser's tor (tor-browser). |

| Field | Value |

| Category | Anonymity networks |

([documentation](https://tb-manual.torproject.org/))<br>`socks`: The bundled tor listens on 127.0.0.1:9150 (default of the tor-launcher code) with flags 'ExtendedErrors IPv6Traffic PreferIPv6 KeepAliveIsolateSOCKSAuth', only while the browser is running. — authentication: None (loopback) ([documentation](https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/applications/tor-browser/-/blob/tor-browser-140.7.0esr-15.0-1/toolkit/components/tor-launcher/TorProcess.sys.mjs))<br>`control-protocol`: ControlPort 9151 (preference extensions.torlauncher.control_port) with cookie authentication; the browser owns the process through __OwningControllerProcess. — authentication: Cookie authentication; the cookie file lives in the browser's data directory ([documentation](https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/applications/tor-browser/-/blob/tor-browser-140.7.0esr-15.0-1/browser/app/profile/000-tor-browser.js)) |

| Node compatibility | None directly. Bitcoin Core's tor.md notes that Tor Browser's proxy listens on 9150; using it for a node only works while the browser is open. |

| Storage | Windows x86_64 portable installer 108 MB (15.0.25). |
| Resources | Similar to Firefox ESR; not measured. |
| Security implications | Downloads are signed with the same Tor Browser Developers key as the Expert Bundle. Tor Browser updates itself, changes its tor version without notice to other programs, and its tor exits when the browser closes, so services that depend on it break and onion services disappear. Routing other applications through Tor Browser's SOCKS port mixes their circuits with browsing. BTCortex must only launch it (for example to open an onion explorer URL) and must never read its cookie or control its tor. |
| Licence | MPL-2.0 |
| Licence notes | Based on Firefox ESR (MPL-2.0) with additional components under their own licences; Tor Project trademarks apply. |
| Integration mechanisms | Detect an installation (default per-user folder 'Tor Browser' on the desktop or chosen path) and the running tor on 9150/9151<br>Launch firefox.exe with an onion URL chosen by the user, for example a local block explorer's onion address<br>Warn when an application is configured to use 9150 instead of BTCortex's managed tor |
| Feasible support levels | External Launcher, Research Only |
| Recommended support level | External Launcher |
| Implementation feasibility | high — Launching is simple; managing it as a daemon is inappropriate by design. |
| Priority | P2 |
| Implementation status | researched |
| In-app catalogue | Yes |
| Notes | Tor Browser's launcher is the reference for how a controller should start tor: '-f torrc', DataDirectory, ClientOnionAuthDir, '--defaults-torrc', GeoIPFile and GeoIPv6File next to torrc-defaults, '+__ControlPort', CookieAuthentication 1 with an explicit CookieAuthFile, '+__SocksPort' and '__OwningControllerProcess <pid>', with DisableNetwork 1 while the network settings are shown. |

| Node compatibility | Transparent: a remote node's RPC, Electrum or web ports become reachable on its tailnet address or MagicDNS name; Bitcoin Core must allow that address explicitly. Tailscale Serve can expose a loopback-bound web UI to the tailnet without changing its bind address. |

Serve is tailnet-only and adds identity headers, so the backend must listen on localhost. Funnel makes a service reachable by anyone with the URL; BTCortex must never use Funnel for node RPC, Electrum or Lightning management interfaces. |

### BTCPay Server

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Category | Payment processors |
| Purpose | Self-hosted, open-source Bitcoin payment processor: stores, invoices, point of sale, payment requests and pull payments, paid on chain or over Lightning straight into the merchant's own wallet, with the Greenfield REST API for integrations. |
| Official website | <https://btcpayserver.org/> |
| Official repository | <https://github.com/btcpayserver/btcpayserver> |
| Maintenance status | active — v2.4.5 published on 2026-10-06; repository pushed on 2026-10-23 and not archived. |
| Superseded by | — |
| Latest verified stable release | 2.4.5 (2026-10-06) — <https://github.com/btcpayserver/btcpayserver/releases/tag/v2.4.5> |
| Verification date | 2026-10-23 |
| Native Windows | no |
| Windows versions | — |
| Windows architectures | — |
| Windows distribution | — |
| WSL2 | likely |
| Docker | official-image |
| Other platforms | Linux through btcpayserver-docker (btcpay-setup.sh installs Docker and Docker Compose when needed), one-click hosting such as LunaNode, cloud and VPS providers (not OpenVZ) and hardware builds. Manual installation and building without Docker are rated very hard and for development; the deployment guide does not mention Windows. |
| APIs and interfaces | `rest`: Greenfield API v1 under /api/v1: GET /api/v1/health without authentication ({synchronized}); GET /api/v1/server/info with any key (version, onion, supportedPaymentMethods, fullySynched, syncStatus[] with paymentMethodId, chainHeight, syncHeight, available); GET /api/v1/stores and /api/v1/stores/{storeId} (btcpay.store.canviewstoresettings); GET /api/v1/stores/{storeId}/invoices with take, skip, status, startDate and endDate (btcpay.store.canviewinvoices; status is New, Processing, Settled, Expired or Invalid, amounts are decimal strings, times Unix seconds); GET /api/v1/stores/{storeId}/payment-methods (btcpay.store.canviewstoresettings; ids such as BTC-CHAIN, BTC-LN and BTC-LNURL); GET /api/v1/stores/{storeId}/payment-methods/{paymentMethodId}/wallet (btcpay.store.canviewwallet: balance, confirmedBalance, unconfirmedBalance); GET /api/v1/stores/{storeId}/lightning/{cryptoCode}/info (btcpay.store.canuselightningnode). — authentication: API key sent as Authorization: token {key}, or HTTP Basic where the user allows it. Keys carry chosen permissions, never more than the user's own, optionally limited to one store (permission:storeId); /api-keys/authorize opens a form in BTCPay that creates a key with the permissions named in the link. ([documentation](https://docs.btcpayserver.org/API/Greenfield/v1/))<br>`http`: Store webhooks: invoice and payout events posted to a URL the merchant sets, signed in the BTCPay-Sig header as sha256=HMAC256(secret, body). — authentication: HMAC signature with the webhook's secret. ([documentation](https://docs.btcpayserver.org/API/Greenfield/v1/))<br>`gui`: Web interface for stores, invoices, wallets, apps and server administration, served by the deployment's reverse proxy. — authentication: User accounts. ([documentation](https://docs.btcpayserver.org/)) |
| Command-line interface | The Docker deployment installs command-line utilities with btcpay-setup.sh -i; btcpay-backup.sh (as root, stops the stack while archiving; BTCPAY_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE encrypts the archive) and btcpay-restore.sh restore a deployment. |
| Remote management | The Greenfield API over HTTPS with API keys and the web interface; the Docker deployment itself is administered on its host, usually over SSH, with its scripts. |
| Node compatibility | Uses NBXplorer as its chain indexer over a Bitcoin full node (Bitcoin Core in the Docker deployment); syncStatus reports each chain's indexer height. Lightning through a node the store connects to (the Docker deployment offers LND, Core Lightning or Eclair). |
| Dependencies | requires: [NBXplorer](#entry-nbxplorer) — Its chain indexer; part of every deployment.<br>requires: [Bitcoin Core](#entry-bitcoin-core) — Through NBXplorer.<br>optional: [LND](#entry-lnd) or [Core Lightning](#entry-core-lightning) — For Lightning payments; the Docker deployment can also run Eclair.<br>optional: [Tor (C tor daemon, Tor Expert Bundle)](#entry-tor) — The server can be reached through an onion service, which server info reports. |
| Networking | The Docker deployment serves the web interface and API behind its reverse proxy on ports 80 and 443, which must be reachable from the internet for its automatic HTTPS certificate; webhooks go out to the merchant's URLs. |
| Storage | Docker volumes for BTCPay, NBXplorer, the node and the databases (PostgreSQL is part of the standard stack); the install example uses the opt-save-storage-xs fragment for a pruned node. Sizes not measured here. |
| Resources | Not measured here. |
| Security implications | An API key acts with the permissions it was given, limited by its user's rights, so a read-only monitor needs only btcpay.store.canviewstoresettings, btcpay.store.canviewinvoices and, for balances, btcpay.store.canviewwallet; btcpay.store.canuselightningnode lets a key use the store's Lightning node, including paying with it. Backups made by btcpay-backup.sh contain secrets and, with Lightning, the wallet and channel.backup: old channel state is dangerous and restoring the archive alone does not recover channels. |
| Licence | MIT |
| Licence notes | — |
| Integration mechanisms | Call the Greenfield API with an API key the user creates with read-only permissions<br>Open /api-keys/authorize with exactly those permissions so the key is created in BTCPay itself<br>Watch /api/v1/health and server info for availability and synchronisation |
| Feasible support levels | Connected Application, Remote Managed, Managed via Docker |
| Recommended support level | Connected Application |
| Implementation feasibility | medium — Connecting to an existing installation is straightforward and needs no software on Windows; deploying one needs Docker on Linux or a hosting provider, which BTCortex does not set up. |
| Priority | P2 |
| Implementation status | researched |
| In-app catalogue | Yes |
| Notes | Other entries of the payments, sidechains and mining scope are still to be researched. |

| Docker | no |
| Other platforms | Go source; Linux and macOS packages historically. |

| Remote management | — |
| Node compatibility | — |

| Networking | Listens on 127.0.0.1:21325. |
| Storage | — |
| Resources | — |
| Security implications | No longer updated by Trezor; keeping it installed means no security updates. HWI, Sparrow and Electrum do not need it (HWI talks HID/WebUSB directly). BTCortex should detect an installed or running standalone Bridge (service or process listening on 127.0.0.1:21325) and advise the user to uninstall it; it must never install it. |

| Licence notes | COPYING contains the GNU LGPL version 3 ('-only' versus '-or-later' not checked). |
| Integration mechanisms | Diagnostics only: detect a listener on 127.0.0.1:21325 or an installed 'Trezor Bridge' entry and recommend uninstalling it |
| Feasible support levels | Unsupported |
| Recommended support level | Unsupported |

| Priority | P3 |
| Implementation status | researched |
| In-app catalogue | No |
| Notes | Search results summarising the Trezor forum say the old Bridge cannot support the Safe 7's encrypted protocol (THP) and that older Model One devices on firmware 1.7.0 or below may not appear in Suite without it; these could not be fetched (HTTP 403/404). |

**Requires verification**

- Statements that the standalone Bridge cannot support the Safe 7 encrypted protocol and the exact deprecation date come from forum posts that returned HTTP 403.
- Whether trezor.io still serves a standalone Bridge installer for Windows was not checked.

| specification | BBQr - Better Bitcoin QR | Deployed Widely (README); public domain (Coinkite) | Splits a file across up to 1295 QR codes. Each frame starts with an 8-character header: B$, an encoding character (H hex, 2 Base32 per RFC 4648 without padding, Z zlib with wbits=10 and no header then Base32), a file-type character (P PSBT, T signed transaction, J JSON, C CBOR, U UTF-8 text, B binary, X executable), then two base-36 digits for the total count and two for the frame index. Receivers must implement all three encodings. The format uses QR alphanumeric mode and adds no checksum beyond the QR code's own error correction. The second animated-QR transport. It is native to COLDCARD Q and supported by Sparrow, Nunchuk Desktop, Krux, Bitcoin Safe and BTCPay Server; SeedSigner decodes only. BTCortex's QR module should support BBQr alongside UR for PSBT import and export and enforce a size limit before decompressing Z-encoded data. | coldcard (COLDCARD Q: display and scan); sparrow; nunchuk (desktop); krux; bitcoin-safe; btcpay-server; seedsigner (decode only, from 0.8.7) | [BBQr README (supporting projects verified 2026-07-27)](https://github.com/coinkite/BBQr/blob/master/README.md)<br>[BBQr specification (BBQr.md)](https://github.com/coinkite/BBQr/blob/master/BBQr.md) |
| BCR 2020-005 | Uniform Resources (UR): Encoding Structured Binary Data for Transport in URIs and QR Codes | Multiple Implementations (two stars in the Blockchain Commons index); document version 2.1.0, revised 2023-08-21 | Encodes typed dCBOR (deterministic CBOR) messages as ur:<type>/<bytewords> strings that suit the QR alphanumeric mode. Long messages are split into multi-part URs (ur:<type>/<seqNum>-<seqLen>/...) carrying a CRC-32 of the whole message. A rateless fountain-code sequence lets a receiver rebuild the message from any sufficient subset of animated frames. One of the two animated-QR transports for air-gapped PSBT signing and account export (spec section 9). BTCortex's QR module must decode and encode UR to exchange PSBTs and descriptors with QR signers. A maintained UR library should be used (developer-tools scope), not a home-grown implementation. | sparrow (hummingbird library); krux (native bc-ur module); seedsigner (UR2 decoder); jade (QR mode: crypto-psbt, crypto-account/crypto-hdkey and bytes; main/qrmode.c); passport (Passport Core: UR 2.0 animated QR, per Foundation documentation); keystone (animated UR QR, per Keystone documentation); caravan >= 1.19.0 (BCUR2 keystore); bitcoin-safe (animated UR QR) | [BCR-2020-005 Uniform Resources](https://github.com/BlockchainCommons/Research/blob/master/papers/bcr-2020-005-ur.md)<br>[Blockchain Commons Research index (statuses)](https://github.com/BlockchainCommons/Research/blob/master/README.md)<br>[hummingbird RegistryType.java (Sparrow)](https://github.com/sparrowwallet/hummingbird/blob/master/src/main/java/com/sparrowwallet/hummingbird/registry/RegistryType.java)<br>[Krux README](https://github.com/selfcustody/krux/blob/main/README.md)<br>[SeedSigner decode_qr.py](https://github.com/SeedSigner/seedsigner/blob/dev/src/seedsigner/models/decode_qr.py)<br>[Jade qrmode.c](https://github.com/Blockstream/Jade/blob/master/main/qrmode.c)<br>[Foundation Passport device features](https://docs.foundation.xyz/passport/device-features/)<br>[Keystone: connecting software wallets](https://guide.keyst.one/docs/connecting-software-wallets-to-keystone)<br>[@caravan/wallets index.ts](https://github.com/caravan-bitcoin/caravan/blob/main/packages/caravan-wallets/src/index.ts) |

Wallets identify outputs by script hash (SHA-256 of the scriptPubKey, byte-reversed hex). server.version negotiates the version; from 1.6 it must be the first message and servers must ignore extra arguments. Core methods: server.version, server.features (genesis_hash, protocol_min, protocol_max, hosts, server_version; 'pruning' is the per-address history limit, unrelated to bitcoind pruning), server.ping, server.banner, server.peers.subscribe, blockchain.headers.subscribe, blockchain.block.header(s) with optional cp_height merkle proofs, blockchain.estimatefee, blockchain.transaction.get/get_merkle/id_from_pos/broadcast, and mempool.get_fee_histogram. Version history: 1.4 removed deserialised headers and added cp_height and id_from_pos. 1.4.2 added blockchain.scripthash.unsubscribe. 1.6 mandated canonical mempool ordering for script-hash status, returned headers as a list, and added a mode argument to estimatefee, blockchain.transaction.broadcast_package (submitpackage) and mempool.get_info; it removed blockchain.relayfee. 1.7 replaced blockchain.scripthash.* with blockchain.scriptpubkey.* (dict results, notifications after reorgs) and added blockchain.outpoint.subscribe/get_status/unsubscribe, blockchain.transaction.testmempoolaccept and mempool.recent; server.ping may also be an unsolicited notification, and hash_function was removed from server.features. The specification also discusses traffic-analysis countermeasures (padding, batching, TLS record padding). BTCortex's Electrum-server health checks and compatibility diagnostics (spec section 7) use it: connect, server.version with a [min, max] range, server.features to compare genesis_hash with the managed node, then blockchain.headers.subscribe to compare the tip height with bitcoind getblockcount. Address lookups in BTCortex's native explorer (spec section 12) are only offered when an Electrum server is connected. Version support differs: Electrum 4.8.2 negotiates 1.4-1.6, Sparrow offers 1.3-1.4.2, electrs supports only 1.4, Fulcrum 1.4-1.6 and ElectrumX 2.0 1.4-1.7.
